bio.content: Olivia Isabel Rodrigo (born February 20, 2003) is an American singer-songwriter and actress. Rodrigo began her career as a child actress, appearing in commercials and the direct-to-video film "An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success" (2015). She gained prominence through her leading roles in the Disney Channel series "Bizaardvark" (2016-2019) and the Disney+ series "High School Musical: The Musical: The Series" (2019-2022). Rodrigo shifted her focus to music and signed with Geffen Records in 2020. Her debut studio album, "Sour" (2021), topped the US Billboard 200 and charts in nine other countries. It was preceded by the US Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles "Drivers License" and "Good 4 U". She was the subject of the documentary film "Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U" (2022). Her subsequent studio albums, "Guts" (2023) and "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love" (2026), produced the US number-one singles "Vampire" and "Drop Dead", respectively. With "Drop Dead", Rodrigo became the first artist to have the lead single from each of her first three albums debut at number one on the Billboard Hot 100. Rodrigo's accolades include three Grammy Awards, five MTV Video Music Awards, and seven Billboard Music Awards. She was named Time's Entertainer of the Year in 2021, Billboard's Woman of the Year in 2022, and ASCAP's Pop Music Songwriter of the Year in 2022 and 2024. Olivia Isabel Rodrigo was born on February 20, 2003, at Rancho Springs Medical Center in Murrieta, California, to Jennifer (née Lee), a schoolteacher, and Chris, a family therapist. She is an only child and grew up in neighbouring Temecula. Rodrigo was born with partial hearing loss in her left ear. She is of Filipino, German and Irish descent and identifies as Filipino American. Her paternal grandparents and great-grandparents emigrated from the Philippines, and her family observes Filipino traditions, including the preparation of Filipino cuisine. She grew up listening to her parents' favourite alternative rock bands, including No Doubt, Pearl Jam, the White Stripes and Green Day. Rodrigo attended Lisa J. Mails Elementary School in Murrieta, where she participated in its after-school musical theatre programme. At the age of five, her parents enrolled her in vocal lessons with Jennifer Dustman, who subsequently entered Rodrigo in local singing competitions. On Dustman's advice, Rodrigo's parents enrolled her in acting lessons. She began taking piano lessons at the age of nine. Rodrigo became interested in songwriting after listening to country music and began playing guitar at the age of 12. In May 2010, at the age of seven, she appeared in an Old Navy commercial. In 2015, at the age of 12, Rodrigo made her acting debut in the lead role of Grace Thomas in the direct-to-video film "An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success". She attended Dorothy McElhinney Middle School in Murrieta for one year before moving to Los Angeles after being cast in Disney Channel's "Bizaardvark" in 2016. She was homeschooled from that time until graduating in 2021. Rodrigo starred as Paige Olvera, a guitarist, for three seasons. In February 2019, Rodrigo was cast in the starring role of Nini Salazar-Roberts in the Disney+ series "High School Musical: The Musical: The Series", which premiered in November 2019. For the series, she wrote and performed the promotional single "All I Want", released in November 2019. Rodrigo left the series at the end of its third season to focus on her music career. Rodrigo signed with Geffen Records in 2020. She negotiated her recording contract to retain ownership of the master recordings of her music. On January 8, 2021, she released her debut single, "Drivers License", which she co-wrote with producer Dan Nigro. The song received critical acclaim and set several streaming records on Spotify shortly after its release. It debuted at number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 and reached number one in numerous other countries. On April 1, 2021, Rodrigo released her second single, "Deja Vu", which debuted at number eight on the Billboard Hot 100. This made her the first artist to debut her first two releases in the chart's top 10. The song later reached number three. Her third single, "Good 4 U", was released on May 14, 2021, and became her second single to debut at number one on the Hot 100. "Sour", Rodrigo's debut studio album, was released on May 21, 2021. It debuted at number one on the US Billboard 200 and spent five weeks at the top of the chart. The album received critical acclaim and was also commercially successful internationally. In June 2021, Rodrigo premiered the prom-themed concert film "Sour Prom" on YouTube. In December 2021, she released a recording of "The Bels", a Christmas song she had written and recorded at the age of five. Rodrigo's commercial success continued throughout 2021. She was the best-selling singles artist worldwide that year according to Billboard, while eight of her songs appeared on the year-end Global 200 chart. "Sour" was the best-selling album globally on Spotify in 2021, while "Drivers License" was the platform's most-streamed song worldwide. The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry ranked Rodrigo as the tenth best-selling recording artist of 2021 and "Sour" as the second best-selling album. To support "Sour", Rodrigo embarked on the Sour Tour from April to July 2022, performing in the United States, Canada and Europe. In February 2022, she signed with Lighthouse Management + Media, entering into a management arrangement with Aleen Keshishian and Zack Morgenroth. The Disney+ documentary film "Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U", which chronicles the making of "Sour", was released on March 25, 2022. At the 64th Annual Grammy Awards, Rodrigo received seven nominations, including Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album for "Sour", and Record of the Year, Best Pop Solo Performance and Song of the Year for "Drivers License". She won Best New Artist, Best Pop Vocal Album and Best Pop Solo Performance. While working on her second album, "Guts", Rodrigo attended a poetry class at the University of Southern California and later adapted one of her assignments into the song "Lacy". On August 16, 2023, Rodrigo became the youngest recipient of the Brit Billion Award, recognising more than one billion digital streams in the United Kingdom. Her second studio album, "Guts", was released on September 8, 2023, and debuted at number one on the Billboard 200. Rodrigo described the album as dealing with growing pains and self-discovery. The album received critical acclaim and was later identified by BBC News as the most critically acclaimed album of 2023. "Guts"' lead single, "Vampire", was released on June 30, 2023. It became Rodrigo's third single to debut at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and made her the first artist to have the lead singles from two career-opening albums debut at number one on the chart. The second single, "Bad Idea Right?", was released on August 11 and reached the top 10 in the United States and United Kingdom. On October 9, 2023, Rodrigo performed songs from "Guts" at an exclusive concert in Los Angeles in partnership with American Express. Proceeds from ticket sales went to her Fund 4 Good organisation. On November 3, she released "Can't Catch Me Now" for the soundtrack of the film "The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes". The song won the Hollywood Music in Media Award for Best Original Song in a Sci-Fi, Fantasy or Horror Film at the 2023 ceremony. Rodrigo embarked on the Guts World Tour in February 2024. The tour ran through July 2025 and included dates in North America, Europe, Asia and Oceania. On March 22, 2024, she released "Guts (Spilled)", a deluxe edition of "Guts" containing five additional songs, including four previously unreleased tracks that had appeared on limited vinyl editions. On April 13, she made a guest appearance during No Doubt's performance at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, performing the band's song "Bathwater" with them. On October 2, she announced the concert film "Olivia Rodrigo: Guts World Tour", which was released on Netflix on October 29. In June 2025, Rodrigo performed at several music festivals. On June 7, she headlined the second day of the Governors Ball and performed a cover of "Burning Down the House" with David Byrne, a founding member of Talking Heads. On June 27, she headlined the 2025 BST Hyde Park festival, with the Last Dinner Party and Girl in Red among the supporting acts. On June 29, she headlined the final day of the 2025 Glastonbury Festival, performing on the Pyramid Stage. Robert Smith appeared as a guest, performing "Just Like Heaven" and "Friday I'm in Love" with Rodrigo. On August 1, she headlined the second day of Lollapalooza Chicago 2025, performing "Buddy Holly" and "Say It Ain't So" with Weezer. Rodrigo also appeared in the documentary film "Lilith Fair: Building a Mystery - The Untold Story" (2025), discussing the history of the music festival. On November 9, she performed "We're Going to Be Friends" with Feist at the White Stripes' induction ceremony into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. On April 2, 2026, Rodrigo announced her third studio album, "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love". Its lead single, "Drop Dead", was released on April 17 and debuted at number one on the Billboard Hot 100. This extended Rodrigo's record as the first artist to have the lead singles from her first three studio albums debut at number one on the chart. "The Cure" was released as the album's second single on May 22, followed by "Stupid Song" as its third single alongside the album's release. The album was released on June 12 and debuted at number one on both the US Billboard 200 and the UK Albums Chart. It became Rodrigo's third consecutive US number-one album and made her the first artist to have the lead singles and studio albums from her first three albums all debut at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and Billboard 200. On April 18, 2026, Rodrigo appeared as a surprise guest during Addison Rae's set at Coachella, where she performed "Drop Dead" live for the first time. On April 30, she announced the Unraveled Tour in support of "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love". The tour consists of 86 dates across North America and Europe, beginning on September 25, 2026, in Hartford, Connecticut, and scheduled to conclude on May 10, 2027, in London. Supporting acts include Devon Again, Die Spitz, Grace Ives, the Last Dinner Party and Wolf Alice. On May 2, 2026, Rodrigo appeared as both host and musical guest on "Saturday Night Live", where she performed "Drop Dead" and debuted "Begged". During a surprise set at Primavera Sound on June 6, she performed her unreleased song "What's Wrong with Me" with Robert Smith. On July 31, she made a surprise appearance during the Smashing Pumpkins' set at Lollapalooza, performing "Thirty-Three" with Billy Corgan. Rodrigo organised Daisy Chain Fields, an all-female music festival held on August 29 in Irvine, California, inspired by the 1990s Lilith Fair concerts. Net proceeds were directed towards charities supporting women and girls. In support of the festival, she released the charity single "Serena Joy", named after a character in Margaret Atwood's novel "The Handmaid's Tale". bio.content: Radiohead is an English rock band formed in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, in 1985. The band consists of Thom Yorke (vocals, guitar, piano, keyboards); brothers Jonny Greenwood (guitar, keyboards, other instruments) and Colin Greenwood (bass); Ed O'Brien (guitar, backing vocals); and Philip Selway (drums, percussion). Since 1994, they have frequently collaborated with producer Nigel Godrich and cover artist Stanley Donwood. Radiohead are noted for their experimental approach, which has influenced the development of alternative rock. The band signed to EMI in 1991 and released their debut album, "Pablo Honey," in 1993. Its lead single, "Creep," became a worldwide hit. Their popularity and critical acclaim increased with "The Bends" in 1995. Their third album, "OK Computer" (1997), is widely regarded as a landmark album, noted for its complex production and themes of modern alienation. Their fourth album, "Kid A" (2000), marked a significant stylistic shift, incorporating elements of electronic music, jazz, classical music and krautrock. Though initially divisive, "Kid A" was later recognised as one of the decade’s best albums. "Amnesiac" (2001), recorded during the same sessions, followed, and "Hail to the Thief" (2003), their final album for EMI, combined rock and electronic music while addressing themes such as the war on terror. Radiohead self-released their seventh album, "In Rainbows" (2007), as a pay-what-you-want download, achieving critical and commercial success. Their eighth album, "The King of Limbs" (2011), explored rhythm through extensive looping and sampling. "A Moon Shaped Pool" (2016) featured prominent orchestral arrangements by Jonny Greenwood. Several members, including Yorke, Jonny Greenwood, Selway and O'Brien, have released solo albums, and in 2021, Yorke and Jonny Greenwood formed the band the Smile. By 2011, Radiohead had sold over 30 million albums worldwide. They have received six Grammy Awards and four Ivor Novello Awards, and hold five Mercury Prize nominations, more than any other act. Seven of their singles have reached the top 10 on the UK singles chart: "Creep" (1992), "Street Spirit (Fade Out)" (1996), "Paranoid Android" (1997), "Karma Police" (1997), "No Surprises" (1998), "Pyramid Song" (2001) and "There There" (2003). "Creep" and "Nude" (2008) also reached the top 40 on the US Billboard Hot 100. Rolling Stone named Radiohead one of the 100 greatest artists of all time and included five of their albums in its "500 Greatest Albums of All Time" lists. Radiohead were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2019. bio.content: Ariana Grande-Butera, better known professionally as simply Ariana Grande, is an American singer, songwriter and actress. She is a multi-platinum, Grammy Award-winning recording artist. Born in Boca Raton, Florida, Grande began her career in 2008 in the Broadway musical "13". She rose to prominence for her role as Cat Valentine in the Nickelodeon television series, Victorious (2010–2013) and in its spin-off, Sam & Cat (2013–2014). As she grew interested in pursuing a music career, Grande recorded songs for the soundtrack of Victorious and signed with Republic Records in 2011 after the label's executives discovered videos of her covering songs that she uploaded onto YouTube. She released her debut album, Yours Truly, in 2013. A 1950s doo-wop-influenced pop and R&B album, it debuted atop the US Billboard 200 and spawned her first US top-ten single, "The Way", featuring rapper Mac Miller. Grande's second studio album, My Everything (2014), continued the pop-R&B sound of its predecessor and incorporated EDM elements. It topped the Billboard 200 and featured four US top-ten singles: "Problem", "Break Free", "Bang Bang", and "Love Me Harder" featuring The Weeknd, the most of any artist that year. Grande's pop-R&B styles extended on her third studio album, Dangerous Woman (2016), which was her first of three consecutive number-one albums in the UK, and spawned top ten hits such as the Grammy nominated title track and "Side to Side". On her next two albums, Sweetener (2018) and Thank U, Next (2019), Grande experimented with trap while maintaining her characteristic pop-R&B tones; being projects with her most creative control yet and showing a more personal and vulnerable side, both debuted at number one in several countries and were acclaimed by music critics. The former won a Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album and spawned the international top three hit "No Tears Left to Cry", while the latter broke several streaming records. Grande became the first solo artist to hold the top three spots on the Billboard Hot 100 simultaneously when "7 Rings", "Break Up with Your Girlfriend, I'm Bored" and "Thank U, Next" did so in 2019. She is also the first artist to have the lead singles from each of their first six studio albums debut within the top ten in the US. Grande released her sixth studio album, Positions (2020) with its lead single, "Positions" debuting at number one in the US and the UK simultaneously. The song became her third number one hit in the US following "Stuck With U" in collaboration with Justin Bieber and "Rain On Me", also in collaboration with Lady Gaga. A deluxe version of Positions was released in February 2021, with four new songs and a remix of "34+35" featuring Doja Cat and Megan Thee Stallion. The remix helped the song peak at number two, the highest-charting song credited to three or more female soloist since 2001 when "Lady Marmalade" performed by Christina Aguilera, Mýa, P!nk, and Lil Kim peaked at number one. The album debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, becoming her fifth album to do so. In April 2021, a remix of The Weeknd's "Save Your Tears" was released featuring Grande. The song reached number one in both the US Hot 100 and the Canadian Hot 100. It spent a total of 69 weeks in the US charts, becoming one of the ten longest-running songs in that chart since its publication. In November 2021, it was announced that Grande would star in the two-part film adaptation of the musical Wicked as Glinda. The first movie released on November 22nd, 2024 to critical acclaim and a worldwide gross of over $750 million, becoming the highest-grossing musical film adaptation of a Broadway musical. Critics praised Grande's performance as Glinda and she recieved over 14 major awards and nominations in the Best Supporting Actress category. Wicked: For Good was released on November 21st, 2025. Ariana Grande’s highly anticipated seventh studio album “eternal sunshine" was released on March 8th, 2024. The title is a reference to one of her favourite films, “Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind” which stars Jim Carrey. The album is a concept album inspired by the events of the film. The lead single “yes, and?" was released on January 12, 2024 and debuted at #1 on the Hot 100. eternal sunshine had a debut at #1 on the Global Spotify charts and on the Billboard 200. The album's 2nd single “we can't be friends (wait for your love)" also debuted at #1 on the Hot 100. During this album cycle, she collaborated with Mariah Carey, Brandy, Monica, Charli XCX, and Troye Sivan on various remixes. Grande has received various accolades, including two Grammy Awards, ten VMAs, one Brit Award, two Billboard Music Awards, and three American Music Awards. All seven of Grande's full-length albums have been certified platinum by the RIAA. Grande has sold over 90 million records worldwide, making her one of the best-selling music artists of all time. Having amassed 98 billion streams globally as of 2021, Grande is one of the most-streamed artists of all time and became the first female artist to surpass 90 billion streams. She was the most-streamed female artist of the 2010s decade on Spotify and Apple Music, and was the only female artist to reach 3 billion total streams on the latter as of 2019. In 2024, Grande became the first artist to have five albums with multiple songs over a billion streams on Spotify. She is the only artist to debut the lead single from all their studio albums in the Top 10 of the Hot 100. Her signature ponytail hairstyle has become an iconic piece of pop culture iconography. In October 2024, she was named the 9th greatest pop star of the 21st Century by Billboard and was the newest artist on the list. Forbes ranked her amongst the highest-paid celebrities in 2019, and Time named Grande as one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2016 and 2019. Billboard recognized her as the "Woman of the Year" in 2018. Her song "Thank U, Next" was in Rolling Stone's 2021 revision of their 500 Greatest Songs of All Time. In 2023, the magazine included Grande among the 200 Greatest Singers of All Time. Grande was nominated in the 2024 GRAMMY Awards for Eternal Sunshine and the Oscars, SAG Awards, Golden Globes, and BAFTAs for her performance in Wicked: Part 1. Recording artists who have cited Grande as an influence or inspiration include Billie Eilish, Chappell Roan, Lana Del Rey, Bryson Tiller, Charlie Puth, Sufjan Stevens, Troye Sivan, Zara Larsson, Tate McRae, Madison Beer, Jung Kook, Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast, Giselle of aespa, and Meghan Trainor. Recently, Grande has been teasing a new full album, "petal", coming out on July 31st, 2026 through Ariana's own label, BabyDoll Music. bio.content: Abel Makkonen Tesfaye, popularly known as The Weeknd (born February 16, 1990 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada), is a Canadian R&B/hip-hop musician, singer-songwriter and record producer. He chose his stage name in tribute to when he was 17 years old, when, along with his friend La Mar Taylor, he dropped out of high school, took his mattress, and "left one weekend and never came home". However, his estranged former producer Jeremy Rose claims the name was his idea. The letter E was excluded to avoid trademark problems with the Canadian band The Weekend. The Weeknd gained widespread critical acclaim for his three mixtapes: House of Balloons, Thursday, and Echoes of Silence, which he later compiled to make a remastered, three-disc album titled Trilogy after signing his record deal with Republic. In 2013, he released Kiss Land, which was considered to be his debut studio album. In 2014, he dropped “Often,” a remix of Beyonce’s “Drunk In Love,” and “King of the Fall.” The Weeknd released two songs in collaboration with the film Fifty Shades of Grey, with Earned It becoming his solo breakout hit. His second studio album became highly-anticipated, with riveting singles like The Hills and Can’t Feel My Face leaving fans hungry for more. Beauty Behind the Madness was released on August 28, 2015. His third studio album, Starboy, was released on November 25, 2016. The Daft Punk-assisted title track led the project as its first official single, released on Wednesday, September 21, 2016, before becoming his third number one track in the United States, as also his home country, Canada. The effort was a commercial success, topping the Billboard 200 albums chart with over 348,000 copies sold in its first week, all eighteen tracks debuting on the Billboard Hot 100, receiving a GRAMMY Award for the Best Urban Contemporary Album, category at the 60th annual ceremony, overall for the second time in his music career and being ranked as the third most popular album of 2017 in the U.S. Next came the My Dear Melancholy EP, released on March 30, 2018 and revolving around his breakups with Bella Hadid during summer of 2016 and Selena Gomez in October 2017. With the lead single, Call Out My Name, the Canadian singer earned the largest first-day Spotify stream count of any song released in 2018 at that time and his eighth Top 10 entry on Hot 100. Tesfaye’s fourth studio album (and his first in three years), After Hours was officially released on March 20, 2020, and is named after a 1985 movie directed by his idol, Martin Scorsese. It was primarily supported by November 2019-released singles Heartless and Blinding Lights, with the pair becoming his fourth and fifth #1 singles in the US and the latter his first #1 single in the UK. The title track and In Your Eyes were also released as singles. Although widely expected to receive multiple nominations for After Hours, Tesfaye failed to receive any nominations for the 63rd Annual Grammy Awards (2021). Tesfaye took to his social media to criticize the Recording Academy, claiming corruption. Speculation arose that the announcement of his then-upcoming Super Bowl performance as well as the discrepancy of being nominated as pop music versus R&B contributed to the snubs. On February 5, 2021 The Highlights was released, as his second greatest hits album. Tesfaye performed at the Super Bowl LV halftime show on February 7, 2021 after announcing he would perform in November 2020. He reportedly spent $7 million on his performance at the show. Despite having a mixed response, the show resulted in a surge in streaming and downloads for Tesfaye's After Hours album as well as for the seven other songs he performed. His fifth album, Dawn FM was released on January 7, 2022, continuing the writing and production work with Swedish pop svengalis Max Martin and Oscar Holter. The album was preceded by the single Take My Breath in August 2021, with Sacrifice announced as the second single. He recently released his sixth album for his 3-album Trilogy, including After Hours and Dawn FM and now Hurry Up Tomorrow . It debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200, becoming The Weeknd's fifth US #1 album and his biggest opening week ever, with 490,500 units. The album also reached #1 across numerous international markets and generated 302 million Spotify streams in its first week. He has continued to donate for charities and humanitarian purposes. bio.content: Charlotte Emma Aitchison (born 2 August 1992), known professionally as Charli xcx, is a British singer, songwriter, and actress. She began posting songs on Myspace in 2008 before becoming involved in the London rave scene. After signing with Asylum Records in 2010, she released a series of singles and mixtapes in the early 2010s. In 2012, she co-wrote and provided vocals for Icona Pop's "I Love It", which became her first number-one single in the United Kingdom and achieved international success. Her debut studio album, "True Romance", was released in 2013. In 2014, Charli xcx was featured on Iggy Azalea's single "Fancy", which topped the US Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the year's best-selling singles worldwide. The same year, she released "Boom Clap", which became her first solo top-ten single in the United States. Her second studio album, "Sucker" (2014), included the singles "Break the Rules" and "Doing It", featuring Rita Ora. From 2015, she increasingly worked with producers associated with the British collective PC Music, developing a more experimental musical style. She released the EP "Vroom Vroom" in 2016 and the mixtapes "Number 1 Angel" and "Pop 2" in 2017. Her third studio album, "Charli" (2019), included the single "1999", a collaboration with Troye Sivan. Her fourth studio album, "How I'm Feeling Now" (2020), was written and recorded during the COVID-19 lockdowns and received critical acclaim. Charli xcx's fifth studio album, "Crash" (2022), became her first number-one album in the United Kingdom and Australia. She contributed the single "Speed Drive" to the soundtrack of the 2023 film "Barbie". Her sixth studio album, "Brat" (2024), became her second UK number-one album and received widespread critical acclaim. The album included the UK top-ten single "Apple", while its remix album produced her second UK number-one single, "Guess", featuring Billie Eilish. "Brat" and its songs received three Grammy Awards: Best Dance Pop Recording for "Von Dutch", Best Dance/Electronic Album, and Best Recording Package. The album's visual style and public reception contributed to a cultural phenomenon known as "Brat Summer". Charli xcx also expanded her work in film during this period, appearing in the 2025 films "Erupcja", "Sacrifice", and "100 Nights of Hero", and the 2026 films "I Want Your Sex" and "Faces of Death". She produced and starred in Aidan Zamiri's film "The Moment" (2026). Her seventh studio album, "Wuthering Heights", was released in 2026 and also served as the soundtrack to the film of the same name. Her eighth studio album, "Music, Fashion, Film", was released later that year. In addition to her solo work, Charli xcx has co-written songs for other artists, including Iggy Azalea's "Beg for It" (2014), Selena Gomez's "Same Old Love" (2015), Will.i.am's "Boys & Girls" (2016), Blondie's "Tonight" (2017), Shawn Mendes and Camila Cabello's "Señorita" (2019), Sigala and Rita Ora's "You for Me" (2021), and Katseye's "Gabriela" (2025). She received the ASCAP Global Impact Award in 2024 and was included on Gold House's 2024 A100 list. Charlotte Emma Aitchison was born in Cambridge, England, on 2 August 1992. She is the only child of Shameera, a nurse and former flight attendant, and Jon Aitchison, an entrepreneur and talent agent. Her mother was born into a Muslim family of Gujarati Indian descent in Uganda and moved to England after the expulsion of Asians under the government of Idi Amin. Her father is Scottish. She grew up in Start Hill, Essex, and spent weekends with her maternal grandparents in Crawley, West Sussex. She attended Bishop's Stortford College in Bishop's Stortford, Hertfordshire. She briefly lived with a friend in Joensuu, Finland, which she later described as a "frightening experience". She has discussed experiencing bullying and discrimination at school, including in relation to her Indian heritage. Aitchison developed an interest in music at an early age, citing artists such as the Spice Girls and Britney Spears as early influences. She began writing songs at the age of 14. She adopted the stage name "Charli xcx" from her MSN Messenger screen name. She later said that she retained the name because she had not thought of another one and did not have a manager at the time. At 14, Aitchison persuaded her parents to lend her money to record her first album, "14". In early 2008, she began posting songs from the project and other demos on her Myspace page. This attracted the attention of a promoter who organised warehouse raves and parties in East London, leading to invitations to perform. She was billed under the name Charli xcx, derived from her MSN Messenger display name. Her parents supported her early career and attended several of the events. Although "14" was not commercially released, she issued the singles "!Franchesckaar!" and the double A-side "Emelline"/"Art Bitch" through Orgy Music in 2008. She later expressed dissatisfaction with this early material. At the age of 18, Charli xcx moved to London to study fine art at the Slade School of Fine Art at University College London. She left the course during her second year to pursue music. In 2010, Charli xcx signed with Asylum Records. She subsequently travelled to Los Angeles to work with producers and met American producer Ariel Rechtshaid. They wrote the song "Stay Away", which she later identified as an important point in the development of her musical direction. In early 2011, she was featured on Alex Metric's single "End of the World". She released "Stay Away" in May 2011 and "Nuclear Seasons" in November. Both songs received "Best New Track" recognition from Pitchfork, with "Stay Away" subsequently appearing on the publication's list of the best tracks of 2011. Charli xcx began working with Swedish producer Patrik Berger, who sent her two instrumental tracks. She wrote "I Love It" and "You're the One" to the tracks. Although she did not initially release "I Love It" herself, Swedish duo Icona Pop recorded a version featuring Charli xcx's vocals and released it as a single in 2012. The song reached number one in the United Kingdom and number seven on the Billboard Hot 100 in the United States in 2013. In June 2012, Charli xcx released "You're the One" as a single from her EP of the same name. She subsequently released the mixtapes "Heartbreaks and Earthquakes" and "Super Ultra". In early 2013, Charli xcx released "You (Ha Ha Ha)" and announced her debut studio album, followed by the single "What I Like". "True Romance" was released on 12 April 2013. It reached number 85 on the UK Albums Chart, number five on the US Billboard Top Heatseekers chart and number 11 on the Australian Hitseekers Albums chart. The album received generally favourable reviews from critics. In May, she released "Just Desserts", a collaboration with Marina and the Diamonds. Charli xcx began developing her second album in 2013. She initially considered recording it in India or France before travelling to Sweden and working with Patrik Berger on a punk-influenced project. The material was subsequently abandoned in favour of a more pop-oriented album. The resulting album incorporated influences from punk and 1960s yé-yé music, as well as artists including the Hives, Weezer and the Ramones. "SuperLove", released in late 2013 as the project's lead single, reached number 62 on the UK Singles Chart and became her first solo entry on the chart. It was later excluded from the album. In early 2014, Charli xcx was featured on Iggy Azalea's single "Fancy". The song topped the Billboard Hot 100, becoming the first number-one single on the chart for both performers. During the same period, Charli xcx received songwriting credits on material by artists including Azalea, Ryn Weaver, Sky Ferreira, Neon Jungle, Rihanna and Gwen Stefani. She contributed "Boom Clap" to the soundtrack of the film "The Fault in Our Stars". The song reached number eight on the Billboard Hot 100 and number six on the UK Singles Chart and was certified platinum in Australia. Her second studio album, "Sucker", was released in December 2014 after its release had been delayed following the success of "Boom Clap". It reached number 28 on the US Billboard 200 and number 15 on the UK Albums Chart. The album's singles included "Break the Rules" and "Doing It", featuring Rita Ora. "Doing It" reached number eight on the UK Singles Chart. Charli xcx has described herself as a feminist and said that "Body of My Own", a song from "Sucker", was written as a feminist statement. In 2015, she appeared in the BBC Three documentary "The F Word and Me". She also opened for Katy Perry on the European leg of the Prismatic World Tour, headlined a UK tour and appeared on Ty Dolla Sign's single "Drop That Kitty" alongside Tinashe. In July and August 2015, she co-headlined the Charli and Jack Do America Tour with Bleachers. A planned second leg was cancelled for what she described as personal reasons. In 2015, Charli xcx began developing her third studio album, describing the project as both her most pop-oriented and most electronic work to that point. She premiered "Vroom Vroom" in October 2015 and subsequently established the experimental pop label Vroom Vroom Recordings. The EP "Vroom Vroom" was released on 26 February 2016, with production primarily handled by Sophie. The release represented a change in musical direction and received mixed reviews. In July 2016, A. G. Cook, founder of the record label PC Music, became Charli xcx's creative director. The single "After the Afterparty" was released in October and reached number 29 on the UK Singles Chart, where it was certified gold. In March 2017, she released the mixtape "Number 1 Angel", which featured collaborations with MØ, Raye, Starrah, Uffie, Abra and Cupcakke and was produced largely by PC Music-affiliated artists including A. G. Cook, EasyFun and Sophie. Charli xcx appeared on Mura Masa's single "1 Night" in 2017. In July, she released "Boys", accompanied by a music video directed by herself and featuring numerous male celebrities. She also performed at the Lollapalooza festival. Much of the material for her planned third studio album was leaked online in 2017, with further tracks appearing in 2018. Following the leaks, the album was cancelled and she began work on a new project. The follow-up mixtape "Pop 2" was released on 15 December 2017. It featured collaborations with artists including Carly Rae Jepsen, Tove Lo, Alma, Caroline Polachek, Brooke Candy, Cupcakke, Pabllo Vittar, Dorian Electra, Mykki Blanco, Tommy Cash, Kim Petras, Jay Park and MØ. Charli xcx subsequently performed shows supporting the mixtape and appeared as an opening act on Taylor Swift's Reputation Stadium Tour alongside Camila Cabello. During 2018, she released the singles "5 in the Morning", "Focus", "No Angel" and "Girls Night Out". On 5 October 2018, Charli xcx released "1999", a collaboration with Troye Sivan and the lead single from her third studio album, "Charli". The song reached number 13 on the UK Singles Chart. Its music video featured references to 1990s popular culture. In 2019, she released "Blame It on Your Love", featuring Lizzo, and "Gone", featuring Christine and the Queens, as singles from "Charli". The album also included collaborations with artists such as Sky Ferreira, Haim, Clairo and Yaeji. "Charli" was released on 13 September 2019 through Asylum and Atlantic Records. In January 2020, Charli xcx was featured on Galantis' "We Are Born to Play", which was used as the theme song for the Japanese theme park Super Nintendo World. She subsequently appeared on 100 Gecs' "Ringtone" alongside Kero Kero Bonito and Rico Nasty. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she announced the album "How I'm Feeling Now". The album was written and recorded over six weeks during lockdown and was developed partly through interaction with fans on Instagram, where Charli xcx shared lyrics, artwork and sound samples for feedback. It was released on 15 May 2020 and received critical acclaim. In 2021, Charli xcx appeared on releases by artists including Elio and Bladee and Mechatok. In September, she released "Good Ones", the lead single from her upcoming fifth studio album. "New Shapes", featuring Christine and the Queens and Caroline Polachek, followed in November. Charli xcx announced "Crash" at the same time. "Beg for You", featuring Rina Sawayama, was released in January 2022, and "Crash" followed on 18 March 2022. In February 2023, Charli xcx announced that she had signed a new recording contract covering her next two albums. She co-headlined the Coachella Festival in April and contributed songs to several film soundtracks, including "Hot Girl" for "Bodies Bodies Bodies" and "Speed Drive" for "Barbie". "Speed Drive" reached number nine on the UK Singles Chart and number 73 on the Billboard Hot 100. She also co-composed the score for the 2023 film "Bottoms" with Leo Birenberg. In 2023, she collaborated with Addison Rae on "2 Die 4" and with Sam Smith on "In the City". In February 2024, Charli xcx performed a Boiler Room set in Brooklyn under the title "PARTYGIRL". The event attracted approximately 37,000 RSVPs, with 400 people admitted. The set featured appearances by A. G. Cook, George Daniel, Doss, Easyfun, Addison Rae and Julia Fox and included previews of material from her forthcoming album. "Von Dutch", the lead single from Charli xcx's sixth studio album, "Brat", was released on 29 February 2024. "360" followed in May, and "Brat" was released on 7 June. The album received widespread critical acclaim and recorded a Metacritic score of 95. Its lime-green artwork and visual style became widely associated with the term "Brat", which was subsequently used in popular culture and media coverage. "Guess" was initially released as part of the deluxe edition "Brat and It's the Same but There's Three More Songs So It's Not". A remix featuring Billie Eilish reached number one on the UK Singles Chart, becoming Charli xcx's second number-one single. "Apple" was subsequently released as a single after gaining popularity on TikTok. Charli xcx also served as executive producer for the soundtracks to the film "Mother Mary" and the television series "Overcompensating". In 2024, she received the ASCAP Global Impact Award and was included on Gold House's A100 list. The remix album "Brat and It's Completely Different but Also Still Brat" was released on 11 October 2024. It featured collaborations and remixes involving artists including Ariana Grande, Kesha, Caroline Polachek, Tinashe, Jon Hopkins, Bon Iver, Shygirl, Bladee, Julian Casablancas, the Japanese House, Bb trickz and the 1975. Charli xcx was named a US ambassador for Valentino Beauty in October 2024 and hosted and performed as the musical guest on "Saturday Night Live" on 16 November. In December, the Financial Times included her among its influential women of 2024. In 2025, "Party 4 U" experienced renewed popularity on TikTok, leading to the release of a music video for the song on 15 May, five years after "How I'm Feeling Now". In June, Charli xcx appeared during Air's performance at the We Love Green Festival in Paris and performed "Cherry Blossom Girl". Later that month, she appeared as Dua Lipa's guest during the London dates of the Radical Optimism Tour, performing "360". In October, she appeared during Addison Rae's debut album tour in Los Angeles. On 10 November 2025, Charli xcx released "House", a collaboration with John Cale of the Velvet Underground. The song was the lead single from her soundtrack album for Emerald Fennell's 2026 film "Wuthering Heights", based on the novel by Emily Brontë. The soundtrack was formally announced in November 2025 alongside the single "Chains of Love". A music video for "Chains of Love" followed later that month, while "Wall of Sound" was released in January 2026. Charli xcx produced "The Moment" through her production company Studio365. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on 23 January 2026 and received a limited release in the United States on 30 January, followed by a wider US release on 6 February and a UK release on 20 February. On 12 May 2026, Charli xcx became the global brand ambassador and a shareholder of the consumer electronics company Nothing. On 24 July 2026, Charli xcx released her eighth studio album, "Music, Fashion, Film", through Atlantic Records. The album included the previously released singles "Rock Music", "SS26", "Wink Wink" and "Camera". An expanded edition containing B-sides associated with three of the singles was released on 26 July. She announced a North American tour in support of the album, scheduled to run from 11 September to 23 October 2026, with Underscores as the opening act. A European leg was announced on 11 September, scheduled to take place from 13 to 24 February 2027, with Audrey Hobert as the opening act. In July 2026, it was reported that a portrait of Charli xcx photographed by Harley Weir during the "Brat" era would be added to the collection of the National Portrait Gallery. On 24 September 2026, she was featured on Madonna's "Danceteria Afterhours". They performed the song together at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards on 27 September 2026. bio.content: Ye, born Kanye Omari West on June 8, 1977, is an American rapper, singer, songwriter, record producer, and fashion designer. He is one of the most prominent figures in hip hop, known for his diverse musical style and polarizing cultural and political commentary. After dropping out of college to pursue a career in music, West began producing for regional artists in the Chicago area. As an in-house producer for Roc-A-Fella Records, he co-produced albums including Jay-Z's The Blueprint (2001) before signing with the label as a recording artist. West's debut studio album, The College Dropout (2004), received critical acclaim and produced the Billboard Hot 100 number-one single "Slow Jamz." He topped the chart four other times with the singles "Gold Digger" (2005), "Stronger" (2007), "E.T." (2011, as a featured artist), and "Carnival" (2024). West's second and third studio albums, Late Registration (2005) and Graduation (2007), both debuted at the top of the Billboard 200, with the latter becoming his most commercially successful to date. Three of his subsequent albums—808s & Heartbreak (2008), My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy (2010), and The Life of Pablo (2016)—were certified triple platinum, while Yeezus (2013) was certified double platinum. Although not as well-received critically as his previous works, Ye (2018), Jesus Is King (2019), and Donda (2021) continued West's streak of consecutive number-one debuts on the Billboard 200. West has also released collaborative albums including Watch the Throne (2011) with Jay-Z, Kids See Ghosts (2018) with Kid Cudi, and Vultures 1 and Vultures 2 (2024) with Ty Dolla Sign. In fashion design, he has collaborated with Nike, Inc., Louis Vuitton, and Gap Inc. on clothing and footwear, and led the Yeezy collaboration with Adidas. One of the world's best-selling music artists with 160 million records sold, West has won 24 Grammy Awards, the joint 11th-most of all time and the most awarded for any hip hop artist along with Jay-Z. His other accolades include a Billboard Artist Achievement Award, a joint-record three Brit Awards for Best International Male Solo Artist, and the Michael Jackson Video Vanguard Award. West holds the joint record with Bob Dylan for most albums (four) topping the annual Pazz & Jop critic poll. Time named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2005 and 2015. West's first six solo albums were included on Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time list in 2020, with the same publication naming him one of the 100 Greatest Songwriters of All Time. West's outspoken views have received significant media coverage. He has been a frequent source of controversy due to his conduct on social media, at award shows, and in public settings, as well as his comments on the music and fashion industries, U.S. politics, race, and slavery. His Christian faith, high-profile marriage to Kim Kardashian, and mental health have also been topics of media attention. In 2020, West launched an unsuccessful independent presidential campaign that advocated for a consistent life ethic. In October 2022, he was widely condemned and lost many sponsors and partnerships, including his collaborations with Adidas, Gap, and Balenciaga, after making a series of antisemitic statements, including denying the Holocaust. bio.content: Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta (born 28 March 1986), known professionally as Lady Gaga, is an American singer, songwriter, and actress. She is known for her image changes and musical versatility and is considered an influential figure in popular music. With estimated sales of 124 million records, she is among the best-selling music artists of all time. Publications such as Billboard and Rolling Stone have included her in lists of significant artists. After signing with Interscope Records in 2007, Gaga gained international recognition with her debut album, "The Fame" (2008), and its reissue, "The Fame Monster" (2009). The albums produced several commercially successful singles, including "Just Dance", "Poker Face", and "Bad Romance", each achieving high sales in the United States. Her second studio album, "Born This Way" (2011), incorporated elements of electronic rock and techno-pop and sold 1.1 million copies in its first week in the United States. The title track was a top-selling song on the iTunes Store at the time of its release. Her third album, "Artpop" (2013), was influenced by electronic dance music. She later collaborated with Tony Bennett on the jazz album "Cheek to Cheek" (2014) and released the soft rock-oriented album "Joanne" (2016). Gaga has also pursued acting, appearing in the miniseries "American Horror Story: Hotel" (2015–2016) and the films "A Star Is Born" (2018) and "House of Gucci" (2021). Her work on the "A Star Is Born" soundtrack included the single "Shallow", which achieved chart success. She received awards recognising her performances, including an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, a Golden Globe Award, and a Grammy Award in a single year. She returned to pop music with "Chromatica" (2020) and "Mayhem" (2025), which included the singles "Rain on Me" and "Die with a Smile". Gaga also continued exploring jazz with "Love for Sale" (2021), her second album with Bennett, and contributed to the soundtrack "Harlequin" (2024). Gaga has achieved seven number-one albums and six number-one singles on the US Billboard 200 and Hot 100 charts. She holds the record for the most-attended concert by a woman and is the only female artist with four singles selling at least 10 million copies worldwide. She was the highest-paid female musician in 2011 and has received numerous awards, including 16 Grammy Awards, 22 MTV Video Music Awards, two Golden Globe Awards, a Sports Emmy Award, and recognition from the Songwriters Hall of Fame. Her philanthropic work focuses on mental health and LGBTQ rights. Gaga is also involved in business ventures, including the vegan cosmetics brand Haus Labs and the non-profit Born This Way Foundation, which supports the well-being of young people. bio.content: Elizabeth Woolridge Grant, known professionally as Lana Del Rey, is an American singer-songwriter and producer. Her music is noted for its cinematic quality and exploration of tragic romance, glamour, and melancholia, with frequent references to contemporary pop culture and 1950s–1960s Americana. With hints at old Hollywood and being young and free, she creates whatever world she wants with some of the best songwriting of the century. She has said she is heavily influenced by some greats, including Britney Spears, Bob Dylan, Frank Sinatra, Elvis Presley, and Nirvana. She has created and amassed a cult following of young fans with her niche and recognizable sound, inspiring a generation of new alternative artists. She has masterfully constructed a world filled with bikers and damsels, staying up til sunrise and living the American dream to the fullest. Throughout her impressive career, she has churned out masterpiece after masterpiece every time managing to create a whole new idea and experience with her songwriting and creative vision. She is one of the best-selling alternative female artists of all time and has nearly 44 billion streams on Spotify alone. She was Grammy-nominated for one of the most critically acclaimed albums of all time Norman F*cking Rockwell! and is also known for her expansive catalog of unreleased songs leaked throughout the years. No matter how much criticism and controversy she seems to find herself in, she continues to always put her artistry first and make stunningly beautiful works. Grant was born in New York City before moving to Lake Placid where she grew up. After struggling with alcohol throughout high school her parents sent her to boarding school for a few years. Once she left she moved in with her uncle and aunt on Long Island. This is when she started learning how to play guitar and sing. She started regularly playing at bars under the name Lizzy Grant and Sparkle Jumprope Queen while she was working as a waiter. During this period she recorded several unreleased demos and EP’s that she used to get noticed by a record label. Sometime in 2005, she recorded the folky Sirens album under the name May Jailer. A few years later in 2008 under the name Lizzy Grant, she signed to 5 Point Records and recorded an EP titled Kill Kill. In 2010 she released her full-length debut titled Lana Del Ray AKA Lizzy Grant exclusively for download that was later pulled from iTunes after financial issues with supporting the album. After getting noticed by what would become her new managers, Ben Mawson and Ed Millet, she switched record labels and moved to England in 2010 where she started working on her debut as Lana Del Rey. She first gained popularity with her music video for the sultry and love-soaked song Video Games released in late 2011. It was released with a homemade video featuring random clips combined with filmed clips of Del Rey singing along to the song. The next single was the title track for her album Born To Die. This song is a perfect way to start off the album with an almost cinematic feeling to it when you first hit play. Following the success of these songs, she released her 2nd EP the self-titled Lana Del Rey in early January of 2012 to build anticipation for her big record label debut. Born To Die was released a couple of weeks later. It spawned the hit single Summertime Sadness which a year later had a Grammy-winning remix that is one of her best-selling songs of all time. The album is filled with catchy lyrics and clever wordplay that draws the listener in. It features motifs of old men she dated, dead exes, and realizing our mortality. It is a baroque pop album with a very hip-hop-inspired beat to it. Going from upbeat songs about living life to the fullest and being wild to slower songs about a past love she missed. Born To Die has gone on to be one of the most influential albums in pop music changing the course of it forever. It is also the second longest-running female album to be on the Billboard Top 200 with over 400 weeks and counting. Towards the end of the same year, she released her third EP Paradise. Promoted with the lead single Ride it has commonly been bundled with her debut album and sold as Born To Die - The Paradise Edition. It features a key part of her music, patriotism. She released a short film titled Tropico soon after that included three of the songs off of Paradise. An EP of the same name was available alongside the film with the three tracks. While she began to work on her next album she kept fans well-fed with a slew of singles including her biggest hits, Summertime Sadness Remix, and The Great Gatsby soundtrack Young and Beautiful. She also sang Once Upon A Dream for the Disney film Maleficent. In 2014 she released her sophomore album Ultraviolence which was mainly produced by Dan Auerbach of The Black Keys. It debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200 marking her first #1. She beautifully executed a sonic shift in her music to a much darker sound. This album started an entire generation of Tumblr sad girls. It was led by the hit singles West Coast and Brooklyn Baby. It also contains the electric guitar-infused Shades Of Cool along with a stunning music video telling the story of an old boyfriend of hers seeing the ghost of her wherever he goes. Ultraviolence dives deep into Del Rey’s abusive relationships with men and also alcohol. It includes a beautifully sung cover of Nina Simone’s The Other Woman. After the success of Ultraviolence, she wasted no time in starting on her next album. Commonly referred to as her best era for aesthetics, Honeymoon was released in 2015. It was mainly produced by Del Rey, Rick Nowels, and Kieron Menzies. She referred to it as her “vanity project” and one she holds close to her heart. Despite being considered her “flop album” it is still one of the best works of her career. It was led with the single High By The Beach which addressed issues about paparazzi and just wanting to “get high by the beach”. Honeymoon is a very jazz-inspired album and also a return to the more baroque-pop of Born To Die and Paradise. With some of her most haunting lyrics, it features the cinematic Honeymoon title track as well as a tribute to David Bowie’s brother on Terrence Loves You. It is her most cinematic album and transports the listener to a beach in California on your Honeymoon or driving down a boulevard in Hollywood lined with palm trees. After some time she announced that LDR5 was in the works. She released the lead single Love which was dedicated to her fans in February of 2017. The album titled Lust For Life came later in July. The album was produced mainly by Rick Nowels and Del Rey like her previous album. This album contained her first features on any of her projects on several different tracks. It is one of her more experimental albums and traced back to her debut album’s roots in hip-hop. She collaborated with rappers A$AP Rocky and Playboi Carti on the track Summer Bummer. She collaborated with A$AP again on the track Groupie Love. The album also contains features with Stevie Nicks from Fleetwood Mac and Sean Ono Lennon, the son of John Lennon. It is a very summery album with some of her most refined and perfected production. The next year she began work on her next album with herself producing as well as new collaborator producer Jack Antonoff who has worked with the likes of Taylor Swift, Lorde, and P!nk. Norman F*cking Rockwell! was released in August of 2019 after a chain of singles. Featuring some of her most epic songwriting and vocals as well as a cover of Sublime’s Doin’ Time, it is her most critically acclaimed album and one of the most critically acclaimed albums in the world with a Pitchfork rating of 9.4, which is the highest score for a female artist this decade. It was her biggest debut on Spotify and debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200. It is one of her most cohesive albums and her fans like to say it is the album she truly found her sound with. It featured themes of feminism, love, and Americana, and encapsulated a perfect beachy summer vibe. It was nominated for a Grammy at the 2019 Grammys in two of the big four categories, Album of The Year and Song Of The Year for the title track. Post-NFR she released a few singles including Looking For America to raise money for a charity, a cover of Summertime - The Gershwin Version, and a Halloween-sounding soundtrack for Scary Stories To Tell In The Dark titled Season Of The Witch. She also released a book of poetry and a spoken-word audiobook titled Violet Bent Backwards Over The Grass. In late 2020 she also announced a covers album of American classics that has yet to be released. After various delays, she released her sixth full-length album Chemtrails Over The Country Club, originally titled White Hot Forever, in March of 2021. It was produced by Jack Antonoff similar to her last album as well as Rick Nowels who she worked with for Honeymoon and Lust For Life. The cover art features Del Rey and her friends gathered around a picnic table in black and white. This album sees her continue to grow and progress as an artist and shows her continue with an alternative sound similar to NFR! While also showing a new folk-inspired country side of Del Rey with the same genius songwriting. The album talks about friends and Americana as well as going into more serious topics. Featuring a very different song for Del Rey with new, rawer vocals we have never heard from Lana before, White Dress is a stunning song about her time as a waitress before her singing career. The album also contains a cover of Joni Mitchell’s For Free with Zella Day and Weyes Blood. Also in the album is an outtake that was originally recorded for Lust For Life, Yosemite. It highlights the same haunting vocals and lyrics as Lust For Life but seems to fit perfectly on Chemtrails as well. She also collaborated with Nikki Lane on this album on the track Breaking Up Slowly, which shows her first venture into country music. In April of the same year, Del Rey took to Instagram to announce the release of another album Rock Candy Sweet. After months the project was never released and instead, three singles from another project were released. Blue Banisters, Textbook, and Wildflower Wildfire. The songs talks about an abusive relationship, taking solace in her friends, and finally a small clue as to why her relationship with her mother is so strained. Finally, she announced LDR8 titled Blue Banisters arriving in October. Another single followed before the release date, Arcadia. This addressed feeling not at home and out of place in California. The album was released in late October and spawned the hit track Dealer. It was her first album since 2017 to not feature Jack Antonoff as a main producer. The album contained several “unreleased” tracks that had been leaked years previously. The album has been said to be her least cohesive project but as always she managed to still deliver a fully baked masterpiece. It goes over topics of body shaming, criticism from the media, abuse, addiction, the pandemic, relationships, and family. It is the most personal project of hers yet and shows a more private side of the usually mysterious singer that we haven't seen before. Soon after she released a beautiful and euphoric song titled Watercolor Eyes for the soundtrack of the hit TV show Euphoria. In December of 2022, Del Rey announced her new album through her website and social media. She released the title track and lead single the same day. Did You Know That There’s A Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd was released on March 24th, 2023. The album was produced by frequent collaborator Jack Antonoff, as well as an array of new producers and sample credits. The record includes the dark and intoxicating track A&W, a nearly 10-minute classic that halfway through drops to an insane trap beat. The record also feature songs like Fingertips, a masterclass in Lana Del Rey songwriting and structure. A loose-cannon of words and thoughts flowing out at rapid speed. The album was critically acclaimed and debuted at #3 on the Billboard 200. LDR10 & LDR11 ARE COMING She is the recipient of various accolades, including two Brit Awards, two MTV Europe Music Awards, MTV Video Music Awards and a Satellite Award, in addition to nominations for Eleven Grammy Awards and a Golden Globe Award. Variety honored her at their Hitmakers Awards for being "one of the most influential singer-songwriters of the 21st century". Read more on Last.fm. bio.content: Adéla Jergová (born 27 November 2003), known mononymously as ADÉLA, is a Slovak singer, songwriter and dancer whose bold pop sound and provocative artistry have quickly established her as a rising global pop figure. Originally from Bratislava, she first garnered attention in 2023 as a contestant on the survival series The Debut: Dream Academy, a global search for a multinational girl group produced by HYBE and Geffen Records. Among over 120,000 applicants, Adéla was selected as one of the final 20 contestants, and while she was eliminated early, executives noted her strong potential for success as a solo artist rather than within a group environment. Adéla began her solo career independently with the release of her debut dance-pop single Homewrecked in September 2024, a confident introduction that showcased her vocal presence and performance skills. She followed this with the electro-pop single Superscar in October 2024, a track that addresses industry exploitation and ambition with sharp lyrical commentary. In February 2025, Adéla released MachineGirl, co-produced by Grimes, blending futuristic pop with introspective commentary on public perception and online narratives. Later in July 2025, she released DeathByDevotion, expanding her thematic range, and in August 2025, SexOnTheBeat arrived with a provocative visual identity that played with hypersexual imagery while critiquing industry expectations. On 22 August 2025, Adéla released her debut extended play The Provocateur through Capitol Records and Polydor Records, distributed by UMG Recordings. The seven-track EP blends pop, house, electronic and hyperpop elements, unifying themes of ambition, exploitation, sexuality and personal agency into a cohesive artistic statement. Critics and publications noted its fearless approach to challenging norms and its fusion of dramatic storytelling with bold sonic textures. To support the EP, Adéla embarked on The ProvocaTour in October 2025, her first headlining concert series. She also opened for American singer Demi Lovato on the It’s Not That Deep Tour in 2026, further expanding her presence on the international stage. In 2026, Adéla entered a new era with the release of KGB, the lead single from her upcoming debut studio album. The track continued her electronic-pop influences while introducing a more personal and reflective approach to her songwriting. KGB became one of her most successful releases, surpassing 20 million streams on Spotify. Later in 2026, Adéla released Red Bottoms, a follow-up single that showcased a more melodic and emotional side of her artistry. Drawing inspiration from 2010s pop while maintaining her signature theatrical sound, the song expanded her musical direction and surpassed 6 million Spotify streams. Both KGB and Red Bottoms serve as introductions to Adéla’s upcoming debut studio album Prima, which releases in September 2026 and is expected to embrace the nostalgic energy of 2010s pop while combining modern electronic production, dance influences and her signature themes of ambition, identity and creative independence. Adéla’s music is marked by candid lyricism, dance-forward production and a willingness to confront industry expectations, positioning her as a distinctive voice within contemporary pop. Her visual and thematic boldness—especially evident in tracks like SexOnTheBeat, MachineGirl, Superscar, KGB and Red Bottoms—reflects a commitment to authenticity and creative autonomy that continues to shape her rapidly evolving career. bio.content: Tame Impala is the psychedelic music project of Australian singer and multi-instrumentalist Kevin Parker. In the recording studio, Parker writes, records, performs, and produces the project's music. As a touring act, Tame Impala consists of Parker (vocals, guitar, synthesiser), Dominic Simper (guitar, synthesiser), Jay Watson (synthesiser, vocals, guitar), Cam Avery (bass guitar, vocals, synthesiser), Julien Barbagallo (drums, vocals), and James Ireland (guitar, synthesiser). The project has a close affiliation with Australian psychedelic rock band Pond, sharing members and collaborators, including Watson, Ireland, and former member Nick Allbrook. Originally signed to Modular Recordings, Tame Impala signed with Interscope Records in the United States and Fiction Records in the United Kingdom in 2015. Parker originally conceived Tame Impala in Perth in 2007. After releasing several singles and EPs, the project's debut studio album, "Innerspeaker", was released in 2010. The album was certified gold in Australia and received positive reviews from critics. Parker's follow-up album, "Lonerism", was released in 2012 and was certified platinum in Australia. It received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Alternative Music Album. Tame Impala's third album, "Currents", was released in July 2015 and won ARIA Awards for Best Rock Album and Album of the Year. Parker received the APRA Award for Song of the Year in 2016 for the album's opening track, "Let It Happen". The fourth studio album, "The Slow Rush", was released on 14 February 2020 and received positive reviews from music critics. At the 2020 ARIA Music Awards, Tame Impala won five awards. The project's fifth album, "Deadbeat", was released in 2025 and received mixed reviews. It included the commercially successful single "Dracula", whose remix featuring Jennie became Tame Impala's first top-ten hit on the US Billboard Hot 100. The origins of Tame Impala can be traced to the Perth music scene. Parker had previously played in several bands, including the rock duo Dee Dee Dums with Luke Epstein. Tame Impala emerged in 2007 as a home-recording project created by Parker, who uploaded several tracks to Myspace. The recordings attracted interest from record labels, and Parker signed a worldwide deal with independent label Modular Recordings in July 2008. To perform the music live, Parker recruited Dominic Simper and Jay Watson, and the group began performing at local venues. Parker chose the name Tame Impala to reflect the project's musical themes, describing it as representing a balance between uncontrolled creativity and refined artistry. Tame Impala's self-titled EP was released in September 2008 following the signing with Modular Recordings. It reached number one on the Australian Independent Record Labels (AIR) Chart and number ten on the ARIA Physical Singles Chart. The songs "Desire Be, Desire Go", "Half Full Glass of Wine", and "Skeleton Tiger" received national radio airplay on Triple J. During 2008, Tame Impala toured as a support act for You Am I, The Black Keys, Yeasayer, and MGMT, and performed at festivals including Southbound Festival, Meredith Music Festival, and Falls Festival. In 2009, the group completed a national "Skeleton Tiger" headline tour, a UK tour, and appearances at V Festival. Tame Impala appeared on Triple J's Hottest 100 list for the first time in 2008, with "Half Full Glass of Wine" ranking at number 75. The song was also included on the associated compilation album. Tame Impala's debut single, "Sundown Syndrome", was recorded at Toerag Studios in London in March 2009 with recording engineer Liam Watson. It premiered on Triple J in May 2009 and was released in July 2009 as a vinyl and digital single, including a cover of "Remember Me" by DJ Blue Boy. The project headlined the first Rottofest festival in August 2009 and later completed a national tour supporting the single. "Remember Me" ranked at number 78 in Triple J's Hottest 100 for 2009. "Sundown Syndrome" was included on the soundtrack of the film "The Kids Are All Right", while "Half Full Glass of Wine" was used in the television series "Entourage". In early 2010, Tame Impala performed at the Australian and New Zealand Big Day Out festival alongside acts including Muse, The Mars Volta, Kasabian, and Rise Against. Tame Impala's debut studio album, "Innerspeaker", was released on 21 May 2010. The album was released in the United States on 8 June 2010 and received positive reviews from critics, with Pitchfork selecting it as "Best New Music". The band toured throughout 2010, beginning with support slots for MGMT's US tour, followed by appearances at Splendour in the Grass, Reading Festival, and headline tours in Australia, Europe, and North America. "Innerspeaker" received four ARIA Music Awards nominations, including Album of the Year and Best Rock Album. On 29 November 2010, it won the J Award for Australian Album of the Year. Tame Impala's second studio album, "Lonerism", was released in 2012 and was mixed by Dave Fridmann. Parker wrote and recorded most of the album himself, primarily at his home in Perth, with additional recording completed in France. The album incorporated a broader sonic palette, more personal songwriting, and a stronger narrative focus compared with "Innerspeaker". During this period, Parker also produced and performed on Melody's Echo Chamber's self-titled album. The first single from "Lonerism", "Elephant", was released in July 2012, followed by "Feels Like We Only Go Backwards". The album was released in October 2012 in Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States. It received widespread critical recognition and was named Album of the Year by several publications and polls, including Rolling Stone and NME. The songs "Elephant" and "Feels Like We Only Go Backwards" ranked at numbers seven and nine respectively in Triple J's Hottest 100 for 2012. "Lonerism" won the 2012 J Award for Australian Album of the Year and received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Alternative Music Album in 2014. The band toured internationally in support of "Lonerism" during 2012 and 2013, including performances at festivals such as Coachella and appearances on "Late Night with Jimmy Fallon". During this period, Watson moved from drums to keyboards, while Julien Barbagallo joined as drummer. In May 2013, Nick Allbrook announced his departure from Tame Impala to focus on other musical projects, and Cam Avery joined the touring lineup. Work on Tame Impala's third studio album began in 2014. Parker recorded material at the Wave House in Western Australia, where "Innerspeaker" had also been recorded. The album's sound moved further towards electronic and pop influences. Parker cited Fleetwood Mac as an influence on the cleaner production style of the album. The album, "Currents", was announced in January 2015 and released on 17 July 2015. The first single, "Let It Happen", was released in March 2015, followed by "'Cause I'm a Man", "Disciples", and "Eventually". "Currents" became Tame Impala's best-selling album, selling more than one million copies worldwide. It received critical acclaim and won ARIA Awards for Album of the Year and Best Rock Album. In 2017, a collector's edition of "Currents" was released, featuring additional tracks and remixes. During 2018, Tame Impala performed at festivals including Mad Cool Festival and Citadel Festival. Parker also collaborated with artists including Travis Scott, Kanye West, Pharrell Williams, The Weeknd, Mike Dean, and Reine Fiske on the song "Skeletons", which appeared on Travis Scott's album "Astroworld". Tame Impala also collaborated with electronic musician ZHU on the single "My Life" and with Theophilus London under the name Theo Impala. Tame Impala began work on their fourth studio album, "The Slow Rush", during the late 2010s. The project was announced as a headliner for the 2019 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival and released the singles "Patience" and "Borderline" in 2019. The album title was announced in October 2019, followed by the singles "It Might Be Time" and "Posthumous Forgiveness". "The Slow Rush" was released on 14 February 2020 and contained twelve tracks recorded in Los Angeles and Fremantle, Australia. "The Less I Know the Better" was voted number one in Triple J's Hottest 100 of the Decade countdown in March 2020. In the same year, Parker appeared on The Weeknd's album "After Hours", producing and providing background vocals for the song "Repeat After Me (Interlude)". At the 2020 ARIA Music Awards, Tame Impala won five awards, including Album of the Year, Best Rock Album, Best Group, Engineer of the Year, and Producer of the Year. In 2021 and 2022, Tame Impala released additional material related to "The Slow Rush", including the deluxe edition "The Slow Rush B-Sides and Remixes". In 2022, the project released "Turn Up the Sunshine", a collaboration with Diana Ross, for the soundtrack album of the film "Minions: The Rise of Gru". Tame Impala also appeared on Gorillaz's song "New Gold". During 2023 and 2024, Tame Impala contributed to several collaborations and soundtracks. The project released "Wings of Time" for the soundtrack of the film "Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves" and collaborated with Thundercat on "No More Lies". Tame Impala also released "Journey to the Real World" for the soundtrack album of the film "Barbie". In 2024, the project collaborated with Justice on the singles "One Night/All Night" and "Neverender" from the album "Hyperdrama". Parker also co-wrote and produced Dua Lipa's album "Radical Optimism" and joined Lipa onstage during her 2024 Glastonbury Festival performance. In May 2024, Sony Music Publishing acquired the catalog of Tame Impala from Parker, covering previous and future works. Parker also confirmed that work had begun on the project's fifth studio album. In 2025, he continued performing live appearances, including a guest performance during Dua Lipa's "Radical Optimism Tour". The fifth Tame Impala album, "Deadbeat", was announced in September 2025 and released on 17 October 2025. The album incorporated influences from house music and the rave scene of Western Australia and received mixed reviews from critics. The single "Dracula" was released in 2025, followed by a remix featuring South Korean singer Jennie in February 2026. The remix became Tame Impala's first song to reach the top ten of the US Billboard Hot 100 and the Billboard Global 200.
