bio.content: Arctic Monkeys are an alternative rock band formed in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England in 2002 after meeting at Stocksbridge High School. The band consists of Alex Turner (vocals, guitar, piano), Jamie Cook (guitar), Nick O'Malley (backing vocals, bass) and Matt Helders (drums, vocals). Founding bassist Andy Nicholson left in 2006. They are one of the first bands to come to public attention via the Internet via MySpace, despite none of them having an account. Their rise to success started in late 2004/early 2005 when demo songs that had been handed out in CD form at gigs found their way onto the internet. These demos rapidly spread among message boards and friends leading to a growing fan base for the band, and were collected on the unofficial Beneath the Boardwalk, which the band recognizes on their website. The band owe much of their success to viral buzz via the Internet, and have eschewed typical 'commercial' channels, including refusing to appear on the UK's (now discontinued) Top Of The Pops music program, which was often seen as a gateway to success. The band's debut album, Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not, held the record for the largest first week sales of a debut album in the UK (in its first week, it sold more than the rest of the Top 20 albums combined). The album sold over 360,000 copies in its first week, but lost the title in November 2007 to Leona Lewis's album Spirit.. It also won the 2006 Mercury Prize, was chosen as the best album of year 2006 by Q Magazine, and received a slew of other accolades. On 19th June 2006 the band officially announced that founding member and bassist Andy Nicholson had left the band after missing the American leg of their tour due to 'fatigue' and the other band members couldn't stand the constant 'missing his girlfriend syndrome' so they told him to sling his hook. Former Dodgems bassist Nick O'Malley was initially brought in as a stand-in, and played the band's remaining summer commitments. He was then announced as Nicholson's permanent replacement. The band's second album, Favourite Worst Nightmare, was released on 23 April 2007, a week after the release of accompanying single "Brianstorm"". Like the first album, this one quickly reached No. 1 in the album charts. Alex Turner described the songs as "very different from last time", adding that the sound of some tracks are "a bit full-on". A secret gig played at Sheffield's Leadmill on 10 February 2007, debuted seven new songs (six from Favourite Worst Nightmare and one other). Early reviews of the release were positive and described it as "very, very fast and very, very loud". The band recorded half of the third album, Humbug at Rancho De La Luna recording sessions with Josh Homme of Queens of the Stone Age in early autumn, 2008, and half in the New York sessions with James Ellis Ford, their producer, in spring, 2009, following their January tour of New Zealand and Australia. During this tour, lead single "Crying Lightning", along with Humbug songs "Pretty Visitors", "Dangerous Animals" and "Potion Approaching" (then known as "Go-Kart"), was debuted live. It was later revealed by Matt Helders in a video diary that the album would consist of 14 tracks and that Turner would stay in New York to oversee the mixing of the material. However, the final track listing, revealed on 1 June 2009, listed only 10. NME reported in May 2011 that the band were teaming up with producer James Ellis Ford once again and would be releasing their fourth studio album, Suck It And See, in late spring at the earliest. Q magazine reported that the fourth Arctic Monkeys album would be of a "more accessible vintage" than Humbug. Q printed edition 299 states "It's the sound of a band drawing back the curtains and letting the sunshine in". The album was recorded in Sound City Studios in Los Angeles in 2010 and 2011. On 4 March 2011, the band premiered on its website a new track called "Brick By Brick" with lead vocals by Matt Helders. Helders explained that this is not a single, just a tease of what is coming and that is it is going to be on the fourth album. On 10 March 2011 the band revealed the album name and was released on 6 June 2011. The album's first single, titled "Don't Sit Down 'Cause I've Moved Your Chair" was released as a digital download on 12 April and on vinyl with ""Brick By Brick" on 16 April for Record Store Day. On 27 February 2012, the band released a new song titled "R U Mine" on their YouTube channel, serving as the bands lead single for their fifth studio album AM, despite it was originally going to be a stand alone single. AM has received critical acclaim from music critics, upon the release of AM on 9 September 2013, the album debuted at number 1 in the UK album charts, selling over 157,000 copies in its first week. The album received widespread critical acclaim and brought Arctic Monkeys their third nomination for the Mercury Prize. The album also won the Brit award for Best British Album. In the United States, the album sold 42,000 copies in its first week and debuted at number six on the Billboard 200 chart, becoming the band's highest-charting album in the United States. In December 2016, Turner confirmed to BBC Radio Sheffield that the band's hiatus had ended and work had begun on their sixth studio album. The album had begun recording in September 2017.The album, Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino was released on 11 May 2018. It's their first concept album, about being a hotel on the moon. Following its release, the album was promoted by the singles "Four Out Of Five" and "Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino". This album had a massive change in sound compared to their first five albums, being slower and more piano based. On 8 December 2021, the band was announced as the Saturday co-headliner of the 2022 Reading and Leeds Festival. On 23 August 2022 at the Zurich Openair festival, they debuted new song "I Ain't Quite Where I Think I Am" The following day they announced their seventh studio album, The Car, which was released on 21 October 2022. On 30 August 2022, they released the first single from the album, "There'd Better Be A Mirrorball", accompanied by a video directed by Turner. The Car peaked at No. 2 on the UK Albums Chart, behind Midnights by Taylor Swift, being their first ever album to not debut at No.1 in the UK. In the US, the album landed at No. 6 on the Billboard 200. Lead singer/songwriter Alex Turner started a two-man project with the former singer/guitarist from the Rascals and guitarist of The Little Flames, Miles Kane. The band is called 'The Last Shadow Puppets'. bio.content: Tyler Gregory Okonma (born on March 6, 1991 in Hawthorne, California, USA) also known as Tyler, The Creator, is a Grammy award-winning American rapper, singer, record producer, director, fashion designer, and the head of his independent record label, Odd Future Records. He was the leader of the now-defunct Los Angeles hip-hop collective Odd Future Wolf Gang Kill Them All (OFWGKTA). Since his first recordings had debuted on The Odd Future Tape in 2007, he had rapped on, and produced for, nearly every OFWGKTA release. Tyler, The Creator is Okonma's most commonly used alias, and the one that both of his first two albums are credited to, but he has used several others as well, including Wolf Haley, Ace (or Ace Creator), and Young N***a, the latter of which was part of a prank on OFWGKTA's official site. Many other characters or alter egos and names are featured in his music, such as Tron Cat, a therapist called Dr. TC, and most recently, Tyler Baudelaire, the character from the 2021 album CALL ME IF YOU GET LOST. He self-released his debut mixtape Bastard (released December 25, 2009) as a free download off of the official OFWGKTA website in 2009. Two music videos were released for tracks off of Bastard, "VCR" and "French!," both of which were directed by Tyler (credited as Wolf Haley). The album is focused on dialogues between Tyler and Dr. TC, and it received generally positive reviews from critics and blogs alike. After signing to XL Recordings in February 2011, he released "Yonkers," the lead single off his sophomoric album "Goblin" (released May 10, 2011), which was released on May 10, 2011. The music video for "Yonkers" (directed by Tyler credited as Wolf Haley) won Tyler The 2011 MTV Video Music Award for "Best New Artist," as well as a nomination for Video of the Year (which lost to Katy Perry's "Firework"). Goblin (May 10, 2011), an album described as "dark," "monolithic," and "a natural sequel to B*stard," continues the sessions with Tyler's fictional therapist, with Tyler venting to Dr. TC about fame, message boards, critics, hype, expectations, media scrutiny, and the idea of being a role model. All of the production was handled by Tyler, save for "Transylvania," which was produced by fellow OFWGKTA member Left Brain. Released April 2, 2013, Tyler's third studio album, "Wolf" (April 2, 2013), moved the focus toward production while still showcasing his rapping. He alluded to several possible track names on his Formspring account, and he stated that the album would focus less on rapping and more on production. In an interview with DJ Semtex, he confirmed that he would handle all the production on the album, except for one song produced by Left Brain, the same approach that was used for Goblin. February 14, 2013 saw OFWGKTA upload a video to their YouTube account, which included L-Boy skydiving and stating that on April 2, 2013 Tyler revealed three album covers via his Instagram. The first single from the album was released on February 14, 2013, titled "Domo 23" along with the music video which features cameos from Domo Genesis, Earl Sweatshirt, Jasper Dolphin and Taco Bennett. On February 26, 2013, Tyler performed the songs "Domo23" and "Treehome95" on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon. Released on April 13, 2015, Tyler's fourth studio album, "Cherry Bomb" (April 13, 2015), marked a significant departure from his earlier works, experimenting heavily with distortion, unorthodox song structures, and influences from jazz and funk. The record pushed textures and volume to the foreground, trading polished hooks for raw, abrasive production that divided critics and listeners. Tracks like "Smuckers" showcased Tyler's ability to pull in high-profile collaborators such as Kanye West and Lil Wayne, while other songs revealed his growing interest in melodic arrangements and risky sonic decisions. Though the chaotic production drew mixed reviews, many noted that Cherry Bomb made clear Tyler was willing to defy expectations and push himself into new creative territory, laying groundwork for the more melodic work that followed. Tyler released "Flower Boy" (July 21, 2017) in 2017, a deeply personal and introspective album that explored themes of identity, self-discovery, and loneliness. The project expanded Tyler's palette with lush, sun-soaked production and carefully arranged melodies, balancing vulnerability with moments of swagger. Songs such as "See You Again" (featuring Kali Uchis), "911/Mr. Lonely," and "Glitter" highlighted a newfound melodic confidence, while tracks like "Who Dat Boy" and "I Ain't Got Time!" kept his sharper, more confrontational side in view. Critics praised Flower Boy for its emotional honesty, detailed production, and clear artistic growth, with many calling it a breakthrough that recontextualized Tyler as both a songwriter and a producer. The surprise late-2018 release Music Inspired by Illumination & Dr. Seuss' The Grinch (November 16, 2018) found Tyler leaning into whimsy and soundtrack-minded writing. Short and thematically tied to the film, the EP let Tyler play with holiday motifs and cinematic cues while retaining his distinctive melodic sense. Tracks like "Lights On" and "Hot Chocolate" provided brief, charming detours that showed how effortlessly he could adapt his sound to different moods and formats. The release of "IGOR" on May 17, 2019 (May 17, 2019) marked a new peak in Tyler's artistic evolution. The album is a cohesive, concept-driven work that blends hip-hop, R&B, soul, and electronic elements into a single emotional arc about heartbreak, jealousy, and acceptance. Tyler leaned heavily into unconventional arrangements, warped synths, layered vocal textures, and inventive transitions that turned IGOR into an immersive listening experience rather than a collection of singles. Standout tracks like "EARFQUAKE" married pop accessibility to experimental production, and the album's overall unity and boldness earned widespread critical acclaim. IGOR's success culminated with Best Rap Album at the 2020 Grammy Awards, cementing Tyler's reputation as a forward-thinking producer and auteur. Tyler released "Call Me If You Get Lost" (June 25, 2021) in 2021, an album that celebrated his love for travel, luxury, and self-reflection. Hosted by DJ Drama, the project adopted a mixtape energy while delivering tightly produced, cinematic tracks that showcased Tyler's storytelling and bravado. Songs like "LUMBERJACK," "WUSYANAME," and "SWEET / I THOUGHT YOU WANTED TO DANCE" displayed his range—shifting from hard-hitting rap to tender croons—while the album's persona work and clever sequencing gave it a clear identity. The record debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, won Best Rap Album at the 2022 Grammy Awards, and reinforced Tyler's ability to craft albums that are both adventurous and widely accessible. Tyler expanded Call Me If You Get Lost in 2023 with The Estate Sale (released March 31, 2023), a deluxe edition that included new tracks such as "DOGTOOTH," "SORRY NOT SORRY," and "WHARF TALK." These additions offered further insight into Tyler's artistic journey and were met with enthusiasm by fans and critics alike. Tyler surprised fans in 2024 with "CHROMAKOPIA" (released October 28, 2024), an ambitious project blending vibrant visuals, experimental sounds, and narrative-driven tracks. The project leaned into color and atmosphere, pairing adventurous production choices with moments of direct, character-driven lyricism. While details about every song continued to emerge, CHROMAKOPIA made clear Tyler's commitment to evolving his aesthetic and presentation, marrying visual spectacle to inventive musical choices. Tyler again surprised fans in 2025 with "DON'T TAP THE GLASS" (released July 21, 2025). Having established larger themes across his previous albums, Tyler would tweet before the project's release that "yall better get them expectations and hopes down this aint no concept nothing". The album combines hip-hop, dance, house, and aspects of funk, pairing club-ready production with Tyler's knack for melody and character. High-profile features from Pharrell Williams, Madison McFerrin, and Yebba helped broaden the album's sonic palette, and reviews noted it as another bold step in Tyler's ongoing reinvention. Over the years, Tyler's popularity has skyrocketed, transcending his origins in underground hip-hop with Odd Future. His influence now extends beyond music to fashion, film, and art. With ventures like Golf Wang and Golf le Fleur, as well as directing music videos and commercials, Tyler has become a cultural icon. His ability to reinvent himself with each project has earned him a devoted fan base and respect as one of the most dynamic artists of his generation. bio.content:
Deftones is an American alternative metal band formed in Sacramento, California, in 1988. The band was founded by vocalist Chino Moreno, guitarist Stephen Carpenter and drummer Abe Cunningham. Bassist Chi Cheng and keyboardist and turntablist Frank Delgado joined in 1990 and 1999, respectively.

After establishing its lineup in 1994, Deftones signed a recording contract with Maverick Records and released its debut album, "Adrenaline", in 1995. Extensive touring and word-of-mouth promotion helped the band build a dedicated fan base. Its second album, "Around the Fur" (1997), was certified platinum in the United States. The third album, "White Pony" (2000), marked a shift from the band's earlier aggressive sound towards a more experimental approach. Its song "Elite" won the Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance. The self-titled fourth album, "Deftones", was released in 2003 and debuted at number two on the US Billboard 200. The fifth studio album, "Saturday Night Wrist" (2006), was recorded amid creative tensions and personal difficulties within the band, some of which influenced its material.

In 2008, while Deftones was recording its sixth album, provisionally titled "Eros", Cheng was seriously injured in a car accident and remained in a minimally conscious state until his death from cardiac arrest in 2013. Following the accident, the band suspended work on "Eros" and recruited former Quicksand bassist Sergio Vega as Cheng's replacement. Vega left the band in early 2021. Since 2010, Deftones has released five studio albums: "Diamond Eyes" (2010), "Koi No Yokan" (2012), "Gore" (2016), "Ohms" (2020) and "Private Music" (2025).

Carpenter, Moreno and Cunningham were childhood friends who attended C. K. McClatchy High School in Sacramento. They maintained their friendship through the city's skateboarding scene. Carpenter developed an interest in heavy metal, while Moreno was influenced by hardcore punk bands such as Bad Brains and post-punk and new wave groups including Depeche Mode and the Cure. After discovering Carpenter's guitar-playing abilities, Moreno arranged a jam session with him and Cunningham, who played drums. The three began rehearsing regularly in Carpenter's garage around 1988.

Carpenter sustained serious injuries after being struck by a car while skateboarding at the age of 15. During several months of recovery in a wheelchair, he taught himself guitar by playing along to recordings by thrash metal bands such as Anthrax, Stormtroopers of Death and Metallica. A widely circulated story claimed that a financial settlement from the accident enabled the band to purchase its initial equipment, but Cunningham subsequently denied the account in a 2007 interview.

The group initially recruited bassist Dominic Garcia, forming a four-piece lineup. When Cunningham left to join another Sacramento band, Phallucy, Garcia switched to drums. Cheng subsequently joined as bassist, and the band recorded a four-track demo. John Taylor replaced Garcia on drums in 1991, before Cunningham returned in 1993.

During its early years, Deftones performed at local clubs and gradually expanded its touring activities to San Francisco and Los Angeles, sharing stages with bands such as Korn. Following a performance in Los Angeles, the band attracted the attention of a representative from Maverick Records. After performing three songs for label executives Freddy DeMann and Guy Oseary, Deftones secured a recording contract.

Carpenter coined the band's name by combining the hip-hop slang term "def", as used in names such as Def Jam, with the suffix "-tones". The name also incorporates a pun on the term "tone deaf".

Deftones recorded its debut album, "Adrenaline", at Bad Animals Studio in Seattle, Washington. Produced by the band and Terry Date, it was released on October 3, 1995. Date subsequently produced the band's next three albums. Although initially achieving limited commercial success, "Adrenaline" gained a following through extensive touring, word-of-mouth recommendations and internet promotion. It eventually sold more than 220,000 copies and became associated with the 1990s nu metal movement.

An early song, "Teething", which was not included on the album, appeared on the soundtrack of the 1996 film "The Crow: City of Angels". The band also appeared performing the song during a festival scene in the film.

"Adrenaline" spent 21 weeks on the Billboard Heatseekers chart, peaking at number 23. Cheng attributed the album's success to the band's perseverance and commitment to its music. Cunningham later described the recording sessions as an experience in which the relatively inexperienced band was primarily enthusiastic about making its first record, rather than extensively refining the songs. Moreno recalled that the album was recorded quickly and that he performed his vocals live in the studio with the rest of the band, using a handheld Shure SM58 microphone.

AllMusic's review praised the album's musical control, precision, rhythmic groove and Cunningham's drumming, while noting similarities between some of Moreno's whispered vocal melodies. The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) certified "Adrenaline" gold on July 7, 1999, and platinum on September 23, 2008.

Deftones recorded its second studio album, "Around the Fur", at Studio Litho in Seattle, with Date again serving as producer. Released on October 28, 1997, the album was dedicated to Dana Wells, the late stepson of musician Max Cavalera, formerly of Sepultura and subsequently of Soulfly and Cavalera Conspiracy. Cavalera also collaborated on "Headup", a song written in Wells' memory. Although not yet a full-time member, Delgado received audio credits on five tracks. Cunningham's wife, Annalynn, provided guest vocals on "MX".

In a 1998 interview with Chart magazine, Moreno explained that the band had entered the recording sessions without a predetermined musical direction. He described the album as having developed organically during the studio process. The band devoted more attention to production and experimented with different drum sounds, including the use of various snare drums. The album expanded upon the dynamics of its predecessor, incorporating contrasts between loud and quiet passages, distinctive vocal performances and a prominent rhythm section.

Contemporary and retrospective reviews praised the album's dynamic arrangements, track sequencing, vocals and instrumental performances. AllMusic's Stephen Thomas Erlewine observed that the album indicated the band was approaching a more distinctive musical identity.

"Around the Fur" increased Deftones' prominence in the alternative metal scene, supported by radio and MTV airplay for the singles "My Own Summer (Shove It)" and "Be Quiet and Drive (Far Away)". The album debuted at number 29 on the Billboard 200, selling 43,000 copies in its first week, and remained on the chart for 17 weeks. The band subsequently toured extensively, appearing at the Warped Tour in the United States, New Zealand and Australia, as well as the Pinkpop Festival, Roskilde Festival and Ozzfest. A live extended play was released on June 22, 1999.

The RIAA certified "Around the Fur" gold on June 24, 1999, and platinum on June 7, 2011. "My Own Summer (Shove It)" also appeared on the soundtrack album "The Matrix: Music from the Motion Picture", released on March 30, 1999.

Deftones released its third studio album, "White Pony", on June 20, 2000. Produced by the band and Date, it was recorded at Record Plant in Sausalito, California, and Larrabee Sound Studios in West Hollywood. The album marked a significant development in the band's musical direction, incorporating experimental arrangements, atmospheric soundscapes and a broader range of vocal and instrumental textures. Delgado, now a full-time member, contributed additional electronic elements, while Moreno expanded his role by playing guitar on several tracks.

The album included "Teenager", a song Moreno described as a love song, which differed considerably from the band's earlier material. DJ Crook, Moreno's friend and collaborator in the side project Team Sleep, handled programming. "Passenger" featured Tool vocalist Maynard James Keenan, while Rodleen Getsic provided vocals on the refrain of "Knife Prty".

Following an extended break from touring, the band spent approximately four months writing and recording "White Pony", its longest studio process at the time. In an interview with Alternative Press, Moreno identified the writing of "Change (In the House of Flies)" as a turning point in the sessions, when the members began working more cohesively. Despite external pressure to release the album earlier, the band chose to continue developing the material. Moreno also adopted a different lyrical approach, incorporating fictional narratives, dialogue and fantasy elements rather than relying primarily on personal experiences.

The original edition of "White Pony" contained 11 tracks, beginning with "Feiticeira" and ending with "Pink Maggit", and featured grey cover artwork. A limited edition of 50,000 copies in black-and-red jewel cases included an additional track, "The Boy's Republic". The band subsequently recorded "Back to School (Mini Maggit)", a rap-influenced reinterpretation of "Pink Maggit". Released as a single, it was added as the opening track of a revised edition of "White Pony" on October 3, 2000. The reissue featured white cover artwork and retained "Pink Maggit" as its closing track.

Moreno expressed reservations about reissuing the album with an additional song, but the band arranged for "Back to School (Mini Maggit)" to be made available as a free download to purchasers of the original edition. The reissue also reflected the band's desire to reach listeners who had already acquired the album.

"White Pony" debuted at number three on the Billboard 200, selling 178,000 copies in its first week. Critics generally praised the album's experimental direction, musical development and Moreno's lyrics. AllMusic described the record as a departure from the band's established sound, incorporating softer and more varied musical elements. The album sold more than 1.3 million copies in the United States and was certified platinum by the RIAA on July 17, 2002. In 2001, the song "Elite" won the Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance.

Deftones began developing its fourth studio album under the working title "Lovers". The band initially intended to pursue a heavier musical direction, with Cheng describing the project as an opportunity to explore a broader range of styles while emphasising heaviness. Moreno underwent vocal training after sustaining significant damage to his vocal cords during the band's 2001 summer tour.

The band converted its rehearsal space in Sacramento into a recording studio and completed much of the album there. Date returned to assist with production, while musician and producer Greg Wells contributed to the arrangements of several songs. Additional recording took place at Studio X in Seattle and Larrabee Sound Studios in West Hollywood. The sessions lasted approximately 12 months and cost around $2.5 million. Maverick Records imposed financial penalties on the band for missing production deadlines.

In January 2003, Deftones temporarily suspended recording to perform at the Big Day Out festival in Australia and New Zealand. The band subsequently returned to the studio to complete the album. Released on May 20, 2003, "Deftones" debuted at number two on the Billboard 200, selling 167,000 copies in its first week. It remained in the Billboard Top 100 for nine weeks.

The album's first single, "Minerva", received radio airplay, while the second single, "Hexagram", was accompanied by a music video filmed at an indoor skatepark in Simi Valley, California, with fans watching the band perform.

Reviews were generally positive, with critics highlighting the band's musical development and distinctive approach amid changes in the contemporary metal scene. Moreno reiterated the band's desire to avoid being categorised exclusively as a nu metal act. Stephen Thomas Erlewine praised the intensity of "Hexagram" but considered the album somewhat reliant on familiar musical territory. The A.V. Club similarly observed that the album was less consistently rewarding than "White Pony", although its strongest moments compared favourably with other releases in the genre.

On October 4, 2005, Deftones released the compilation album "B-Sides & Rarities". The CD included B-sides and cover versions recorded throughout the band's career, while an accompanying DVD featured behind-the-scenes footage and the band's music videos released up to that point.

For its fifth studio album, Deftones departed from its longstanding collaboration with Date and chose Bob Ezrin as producer. Cunningham explained that the band wanted to change its working methods and explore a different production approach. After recording the instrumental parts, Moreno decided to record his vocals separately. Former Far guitarist Shaun Lopez subsequently assisted with production.

The recording sessions were affected by tensions among band members and difficulties in their personal lives. Cunningham later compared the process to "pulling teeth". The resulting album, "Saturday Night Wrist", was released on October 31, 2006, and debuted at number 10 on the Billboard 200, selling slightly more than 76,000 copies in its first week. This represented a considerable decline in initial sales compared with the band's two preceding albums.

The album's first single, "Hole in the Earth", was released on September 12, 2006. It subsequently appeared in the video game "Saints Row 2" and as downloadable content for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 versions of "Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock". The second single, "Mein", was released on March 9, 2007. The album also featured collaborations with Annie Hardy of Giant Drag on "Pink Cellphone" and Serj Tankian of System of a Down on "Mein".

Reviews included praise for the album's songwriting and overall strength. Blabbermouth.net described it as one of the band's strongest releases. Deftones spent much of 2006 and 2007 touring internationally in support of the album, performing in North America, Europe, South America, Japan and Australia. The band also appeared on the Taste of Chaos and Family Values tours and at the Soundwave Festival.

In autumn 2007, Deftones began writing material for its sixth studio album, "Eros". Moreno described the project as unconventional and aggressive. Recording commenced on April 14, 2008, with Date returning as producer.

On November 4, 2008, Cheng was seriously injured in a car accident in Santa Clara, California. The injuries left him in a minimally conscious state. Following the accident, the band and Cheng's mother, Jeanne, began publishing updates on his condition through the band's blog. On December 9, 2008, Cheng was transferred to a hospital specialising in the treatment and management of traumatic and non-traumatic brain injuries.

In January 2009, Deftones announced that Cheng had not made significant progress in his recovery and that Sergio Vega, formerly of Quicksand, would perform bass duties in his absence. Vega had previously filled in for Cheng temporarily in 1999. On April 5, 2009, the band performed its first concert without Cheng since 1998 at the Bamboozle Left festival in Irvine, California.

On June 23, 2009, Deftones announced that it was indefinitely postponing the release of "Eros". The band explained that the album no longer adequately represented its current musical and personal direction and that it intended to adopt a different creative approach. The decision was also influenced by Cheng's condition, although the band clarified that the postponement was primarily an artistic decision and not directly related to the accident.

Several musicians from alternative metal bands, including Brian Welch and Reginald Arvizu of Korn, members of Sevendust and Slipknot, and other collaborators, recorded "A Song for Chi" to raise funds for Cheng and his family. Deftones also organised two benefit concerts in Los Angeles in 2009.

In March 2009, Deftones fan Gina Blackmore established the website One Love for Chi to provide information and updates about Cheng's condition and to raise funds for his medical care. The site also hosted auctions of items donated by the band's associates, with proceeds going to Cheng's family.

Deftones recorded its sixth studio album, "Diamond Eyes", with producer Nick Raskulinecz. Originally scheduled for release on April 27, 2010, the album was subsequently postponed to May 18. After it leaked online in March, the release date was moved forward to May 4.

The first single, "Rocket Skates", was made available as a free download on February 23, 2010. The title track, "Diamond Eyes", was released as the album's first radio single on March 15. Both songs received positive responses from critics and fans, with reviewers noting similarities to the band's earlier material on "Around the Fur". In contrast to the darker and more aggressive direction planned for "Eros", "Diamond Eyes" featured a more optimistic lyrical and musical approach.

The band toured North America in autumn 2010 with Mastodon and Alice in Chains. The joint tour, titled Blackdiamondskye, took its name from the three bands' contemporary albums: "Black Gives Way to Blue", "Diamond Eyes" and "Crack the Skye". Each concert was promoted with a limited-edition screen-printed poster created by artist Jermaine Rogers, who had produced much of Deftones' concert artwork since the late 1990s.

On April 16, 2011, Deftones released "Covers", a limited-edition LP issued for Record Store Day. It collected cover versions recorded over several years, including "Drive", originally by the Cars, "If Only Tonight We Could Sleep", originally by the Cure, and "No Ordinary Love", originally by Sade. On October 25, 2011, the band released "The Vinyl Collection 1995–2011", a limited-edition box set of 1,000 copies.

In March 2012, Carpenter revealed in an interview published on ESP Guitars' YouTube channel that Deftones was working on its seventh studio album. Raskulinecz was announced as the producer. Reports initially indicated that the band was considering recording several B-sides, including cover versions of songs by Elvis Presley and Earth, Wind & Fire, but the album was ultimately released without bonus tracks.

On July 28, 2012, Deftones performed two new songs, "Rosemary" and "Roller Derby", the latter subsequently renamed "Poltergeist". The band's seventh album, "Koi No Yokan", was announced on August 30 and released by Reprise Records on November 12, 2012. Continuing the experimental approach of "Diamond Eyes", the album explored atmospheric textures, varied dynamics and a broad range of musical styles.

"Koi No Yokan" received widespread critical acclaim. Metacritic assigned it a score of 86 out of 100, based on 18 reviews. In May 2013, the album received Revolver magazine's Golden Gods Award for Album of the Year.

On April 13, 2013, Cheng died at a hospital in Stockton, California, after suffering cardiac arrest. He had partially recovered from his injuries and returned home, but his death occurred more than four years after the accident. In May 2013, Moreno indicated that the previously shelved album "Eros" might be released following Cheng's death.

In March 2014, while Moreno was touring with his side project Crosses in support of its self-titled debut album, the remaining members of Deftones began writing material for the band's eighth studio album. The band had previously indicated that it intended to begin recording in late 2014 or early 2015.

On April 13, 2014, the first anniversary of Cheng's death, Deftones released "Smile", a song from the unreleased "Eros" sessions, on YouTube. The track was the first officially released material from the album. Warner Music Group removed the video two days later because of a copyright claim, despite Moreno having uploaded it. The song was subsequently made available again and remained the only officially released recording from the "Eros" sessions.

In February 2015, after completing the drum tracks for its eighth album, Moreno revealed in an interview with Rolling Stone that the band had written 16 songs. He described the material as more complex and contemplative than that of "Koi No Yokan". In a May 2015 interview with Kerrang!, Moreno characterised the album as featuring a variety of moods, neither entirely positive nor wholly aggressive.

The recording sessions involved greater collaboration among the band members. Carpenter initially experienced some difficulty adapting to the album's direction, but the group subsequently emphasised the collective nature of the songwriting. Vega played a six-string bass, contributing to the album's expanded sonic range. After working with Raskulinecz on the preceding two albums, Deftones selected Matt Hyde as producer. Hyde had previously worked as a recording engineer on "Koi No Yokan".

The album's release was postponed several times from its original September 2015 schedule. On February 4, 2016, the band released "Prayers / Triangles" as the first single. "Doomed User" and "Hearts / Wires" were made available on March 16 and April 3, respectively, ahead of the album's release. "Gore" was released on April 8, 2016, followed by the second official single, "Phantom Bride", on June 7. The latter featured a guitar solo by Jerry Cantrell of Alice in Chains, an unusual addition to a Deftones recording.

"Gore" received generally positive reviews. The Guardian's Gwilym Mumford praised its experimentation and atmospheric arrangements, highlighting the contrast between Moreno's melodic vocals and less explicit lyrics and Carpenter's heavy guitar riffs.

In 2017, Moreno confirmed that Deftones had begun writing material for its ninth studio album, initially targeting a 2019 release. He indicated that the band intended to move away from the musical approach of "Gore" and that he would reduce his role in leading the songwriting to give Carpenter and Cunningham greater creative involvement. In May 2018, Moreno described the new material as considerably heavier than the previous album.

That same month, Deftones embarked on a South American tour with Quicksand and Deadly Apples as supporting acts.

In April 2020, the band announced that it was mixing its ninth studio album. The recording sessions took place in Los Angeles, with Date returning as producer for the first time since the unreleased "Eros" sessions in 2008.

On August 19, 2020, Deftones announced the title and release date of its ninth album, "Ohms". The announcement was accompanied by the album artwork and track listing. The title track was released as the lead single on August 21, followed by "Genesis" on September 17. The album was released on September 25, 2020.

On September 22, 2020, the band launched its "Adopt-a-Dot" campaign, allowing fans to digitally sponsor individual dots from the "Ohms" album cover through charitable donations.

In October 2020, Deftones announced a 20th-anniversary reissue of "White Pony", scheduled for release in December. The reissue was packaged with "Black Stallion", a companion remix album featuring contributions from musicians and producers including Mike Shinoda of Linkin Park, DJ Shadow and Robert Smith of the Cure.

The band's planned joint tour with Gojira in support of "Ohms" was postponed twice because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Poppy, initially scheduled to support the two bands, withdrew following the second postponement. The tour eventually took place in April 2022.

In March 2022, Vega confirmed that he had left Deftones in early 2021. He stated that he had never been an official member but had worked as a contracted bassist throughout his tenure. According to Vega, he had sought formal membership but departed after being offered the same contractual status he had held since joining the band.

In April 2022, Fred Sablan was announced as Vega's touring replacement. Touring guitarist Lance Jackman also joined the band. On May 20, 2022, Jackman was announced as a temporary replacement for Carpenter during the band's 2022 European tour.

In April 2024, Moreno told KROQ that Deftones had completed most of its tenth studio album. He stated that the instrumental recordings had been finished, although the vocals had yet to be recorded.

In September 2024, Deftones announced a North American headlining tour for 2025, its first such tour since 2022. On November 4, 2024, the band announced a headlining performance at Crystal Palace Park in London on June 29, 2025, with Weezer and High Vis as supporting acts.

In March 2025, Deftones was announced as a performer at the Glastonbury Festival, marking its first scheduled appearance at the festival since 1998. The band was due to perform on June 28, 2025, but cancelled its appearance on the day because of an illness affecting one of its members.

On July 10, 2025, Deftones announced its tenth studio album, "Private Music", and released its lead single, "My Mind Is a Mountain", on the same day. The second single, "Milk of the Madonna", was released on August 8, 2025. "Private Music" was released on August 22, 2025, and featured touring bassist Sablan.

bio.content: The Smiths were an English rock band formed in Manchester in 1982, composed of Morrissey (vocals), Johnny Marr (guitar), Andy Rourke (bass), and Mike Joyce (drums). Morrissey and Marr formed the band's songwriting partnership. The Smiths are regarded as one of the most important acts to emerge from 1980s British independent music. The Smiths signed to the independent label Rough Trade Records in 1983 and released their debut album, The Smiths, in 1984. Their focus on a guitar, bass, and drum sound, fusing 1960s rock and post-punk, was a rejection of the synth-pop sound predominant at the time. Several of the band's singles reached the top 20 of the UK Singles Chart, and all their studio albums reached the top five of the UK Albums Chart, including the number-one album Meat Is Murder (1985). The band achieved mainstream success in Europe with The Queen Is Dead (1986) and Strangeways, Here We Come (1987), which both entered the top 20 of the European Albums Chart. In 1986, the Smiths briefly expanded to a five-piece with the addition of guitarist Craig Gannon, but internal tensions eventually led to their breakup the following year. The split was followed by heavily publicized lawsuits over royalties, and the band members have consistently rejected numerous offers to reunite in the years since. Bassist Andy Rourke died in 2023. History. 1982: Formation and early performances. In May 1982, Johnny Marr and his friend Steve Pomfret went to the home of Steven Morrissey in Stretford to invite him to form a band. Marr and Morrissey had met at a Patti Smith gig at Manchester's Apollo Theatre on 31 August 1978, when Marr was 14 and Morrissey was 19. They bonded through their love of poetry and literature. A fan of the New York Dolls, Marr had been impressed that Morrissey had written a book on the band and was inspired to turn up on his doorstep, following the example of Jerry Leiber, who had formed his working partnership with Mike Stoller after turning up at Stoller's door. According to Morrissey: "We got on absolutely famously. We were very similar in drive." The two found that they were fans of many of the same bands. When Marr looked through Morrissey's singles collection, he found the Monochrome Set, a band they both admired. The next day, Morrissey phoned Marr to confirm that he would be interested in forming a band with him. A few days later, Morrissey and Marr held their first rehearsal in Marr's rented attic room in Bowdon. Morrissey provided the lyrics for "Don't Blow Your Own Horn," the first song that they worked on; however, they decided against retaining the song, with Marr commenting that "neither of us liked it very much." The next song that they worked on was "The Hand That Rocks the Cradle," which again was based on lyrics produced by Morrissey. Marr based the tempo on the Patti Smith song "Kimberly," and they recorded it on Marr's TEAC four-track cassette recorder. The third track that the duo worked on was "Suffer Little Children." Alongside these original compositions, Morrissey suggested that the band produce a cover of "I Want a Boy for My Birthday," a song by the 1960s American girl group the Cookies; although he had never heard of the song before, Marr agreed, enjoying the subversive element of having a male vocalist sing it, and the song was recorded on his TEAC machine. "It's still really clear. It was a sunny day, about one o'clock. There was no advance phone call or anything. I just knocked, and he opened the door. As soon as the door opened, Pommy [Pomfret] took two very firm steps back. Which is one of the things that got me to talk so fast; it was just plain exuberance." — Marr, on arriving at Morrissey's door By late 1982, Morrissey had chosen the band name the Smiths. He said later that "it was the most ordinary name, and I thought it was time that the ordinary folk of the world showed their faces." Around the time of the band's formation, Morrissey decided that he would be publicly known only by his surname, with Marr referring to him as "Mozzer" or "Moz." In 1983, he forbade those around him from using the name "Steven," which he despised. After remaining with the band for several rehearsals, Pomfret departed acrimoniously. He was replaced by the bass player Dale Hibbert, who worked at Manchester's Decibel Studios, where Marr had met him while recording Freak Party's demo. Through Hibbert, the Smiths recorded their first demo at Decibel one night in August 1982. Aided by drummer Simon Wolstencroft, whom Marr had worked with in Freak Party, the band recorded both "The Hand That Rocks the Cradle" and "Suffer Little Children." Wolstencroft was not interested in joining the band, so following auditions, Mike Joyce joined; he later revealed that he was under the influence of magic mushrooms during his audition. Meanwhile, Morrissey took the demo recording to Factory Records, but Factory's Tony Wilson was not interested. In October 1982, the Smiths gave their first public performance as a support act for Blue Rondo à la Turk during a student music and fashion show, "An Evening of Pure Pleasure," at Manchester's Ritz. During the performance, they played both their own compositions and "I Want a Boy for My Birthday." Morrissey had organized the gig's aesthetic; the band came onstage to Klaus Nomi's version of Henry Purcell's "The Cold Song" playing through the venue's sound system before his friend James Maker stepped onstage to introduce the band. Maker remained onstage during the performance, relating that "I was given a pair of maracas—an optional extra—and carte blanche. There were no instructions—I think it was generally accepted I would improvise... I was there to drink red wine, make extraneous hand gestures, and keep well within the tight, chalked circle that Morrissey had drawn around me." Hibbert was allegedly unhappy with what he perceived as the band's "gay" aesthetic; in turn, Morrissey and Marr were unhappy with his bass playing, so he was replaced by Marr's old schoolfriend Andy Rourke. Hibbert denies that he objected to the band being perceived as gay and said he was not sure why he was asked to leave. In December 1982, the Smiths recorded their second demo at the Drone Studios in Chorlton-cum-Hardy; the tracks recorded were "What Difference Does It Make?," "Handsome Devil," and "Miserable Lie." This was used as their audition tape for the record company EMI, which turned the band down. The band continued to practice, this time at the upstairs of the Portland Street Crazy Face Clothing company, a space secured by their new manager, Joe Moss. By Christmas, they had written four new songs: "These Things Take Time," "What Do You See in Him?," "Jeane," and "A Matter of Opinion," the last of which they soon scrapped. Their next gig was Manchester's Manhattan in late January 1983, and although Maker would again appear as a go-go dancer, this was the last time that he did so. In early February, they performed their third gig, at the Haçienda. bio.content: Michael Joseph Jackson (August 29, 1958 - June 25, 2009) was an American singer, songwriter, dancer, and philanthropist. Commonly known as the "King of Pop", he was one of the most commercially successful and influential entertainers in popular music. His career spanned more than four decades, during which he achieved success both as a member of the Jackson 5 and as a solo artist. He contributed to the development of music videos as a prominent form of artistic and commercial expression and became associated with dance techniques including the moonwalk, the robot, and the anti-gravity lean. Jackson was born in Gary, Indiana, as the eighth of ten children in the Jackson family. He began performing at an early age and became the lead singer of the Jackson 5, a group formed with several of his brothers. The group signed with Motown Records and achieved commercial success with songs including "I Want You Back", "ABC", "The Love You Save", and "I'll Be There". During the 1970s, Jackson also released several solo albums through Motown, including "Got to Be There" (1972), "Ben" (1972), "Music & Me" (1973), and "Forever, Michael" (1975). After the Jackson 5 left Motown in 1975 and became the Jacksons, Jackson continued performing with the group while pursuing a solo career. His appearance in the musical film "The Wiz" (1978) led to a professional relationship with producer Quincy Jones. Their collaboration resulted in the album "Off the Wall" (1979), which established Jackson as a successful solo performer and produced the hit singles "Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough" and "Rock with You". Jackson's sixth studio album, "Thriller" (1982), became the best-selling album in history. It produced several successful singles, including "Billie Jean", "Beat It", and "Thriller". The accompanying music videos received extensive television exposure and played a significant role in the growing popularity of music video broadcasting. In 1983, Jackson performed the moonwalk during the television special "Motown 25: Yesterday, Today, Forever", bringing widespread public attention to the dance move. During the 1980s, Jackson became one of the most prominent figures in international popular music. He received numerous awards, including multiple Grammy Awards and American Music Awards. In 1984, he sustained scalp burns during the filming of a Pepsi commercial and later donated part of a legal settlement related to the incident to medical causes. The same year, he participated in the Jacksons' "Victory Tour", his final concert tour with the group. In 1985, Jackson and Lionel Richie co-wrote the charity single "We Are the World", which raised funds for humanitarian relief efforts. That year, Jackson acquired ATV Music Publishing, obtaining rights to a catalog that included much of the Beatles' publishing portfolio. He also became known for his support of charitable causes and donations to a wide range of organizations. From the mid-1980s onward, Jackson's appearance attracted considerable media attention. He was diagnosed with vitiligo and lupus, conditions that affected his skin pigmentation and health. Jackson stated that changes in his appearance were related to these medical conditions, weight loss, and cosmetic procedures. Media coverage also focused on aspects of his private life, including his ownership of a pet chimpanzee named Bubbles and his residence at Neverland Ranch in California. Jackson released "Bad" in 1987. The album became the first to produce five number-one singles on the US Billboard Hot 100: "I Just Can't Stop Loving You", "Bad", "The Way You Make Me Feel", "Man in the Mirror", and "Dirty Diana". The accompanying "Bad World Tour" attracted large audiences internationally. In 1988, he published the autobiography "Moonwalk" and released the film "Moonwalker". In 1991, Jackson signed a record contract with Sony Music that was reported at the time to be among the largest in the music industry. He released the album "Dangerous" later that year. The album included the successful singles "Black or White", "Remember the Time", and "Heal the World". In 1992, he founded the Heal the World Foundation and began the "Dangerous World Tour", portions of whose proceeds supported charitable activities. In 1993, his performance at the Super Bowl XXVII halftime show became one of the most-watched halftime performances in the event's history. In 1993, Jackson faced allegations of child sexual abuse involving a minor. A civil lawsuit was settled in 1994 without an admission of wrongdoing. Criminal charges were not filed in connection with the allegations, and investigations concluded without prosecution. During this period, Jackson experienced health problems and dependence on prescription pain medication. Jackson married Lisa Marie Presley, daughter of Elvis Presley, in 1994. The marriage ended in divorce in 1996. In 1995, he released the double album "HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I", which combined a greatest-hits collection with new material. The album included the singles "Scream", a duet with Janet Jackson, "You Are Not Alone", "Earth Song", and "They Don't Care About Us". The accompanying "HIStory World Tour" became the most-attended tour of his career. In 1996, Jackson married Debbie Rowe. The couple had two children, Michael Joseph Jackson Jr. and Paris-Michael Katherine Jackson, before divorcing in 2000. A third child, Prince Michael Jackson II, was born in 2002 through surrogacy. In 1997, Jackson released "Blood on the Dance Floor: HIStory in the Mix", a remix album that also included new material. He later worked on "Invincible" (2001), which was reported to have one of the highest production costs of any album at the time. Its release was followed by a public dispute with Sony Music regarding promotion and contractual matters. In the early 2000s, Jackson participated in several charitable events, including benefit concerts following the September 11 attacks. He also marked the thirtieth anniversary of his solo career with a series of concerts in New York City featuring numerous guest performers. In 2003, the documentary "Living with Michael Jackson" generated controversy due to Jackson's comments about sharing sleeping accommodations with children. Later that year, he was charged with child molestation and related offenses involving another minor. The trial took place in 2005, and Jackson was acquitted on all counts. Following the trial, Jackson spent periods of time living outside the United States, including in Bahrain and Ireland. He faced financial difficulties related to debt and legal obligations but retained substantial music publishing assets. In 2008, he released "Thriller 25", a commemorative edition of "Thriller" marking the album's twenty-fifth anniversary. In March 2009, Jackson announced "This Is It", a planned series of comeback concerts in London. Demand for tickets led to a significant expansion of the schedule. While preparing for the performances, Jackson died on June 25, 2009, at the age of 50 after receiving a fatal dose of propofol administered by his personal physician, Conrad Murray. Jackson is one of the best-selling music artists in history, with estimated record sales exceeding 500 million worldwide. He achieved 13 Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles as a solo artist and received numerous honors, including Grammy Awards, American Music Awards, Brit Awards, and inductions into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, the Songwriters Hall of Fame, and the Dance Hall of Fame. His influence on popular music, music videos, dance, fashion, and entertainment has been widely documented, and his charitable activities included support for numerous humanitarian causes. bio.content:
Billie Eilish Pirate Baird O'Connell (born December 18, 2001) is an American singer-songwriter. She is known for her distinctive musical sound and vocal style and has become a prominent figure in 2020s popular culture. Her production style frequently incorporates harmony lines and layered vocals, extending the technique of double tracking.

Eilish gained public attention in 2015 with her debut single, "Ocean Eyes", which was written and produced by her brother, Finneas O'Connell. In 2017, she released her debut EP, "Don't Smile at Me", which achieved commercial success in several countries, including the United States, United Kingdom and Australia. Her debut studio album, "When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?" (2019), debuted at number one on the US Billboard 200 and UK Albums Chart and was among the year's best-selling albums. Its single "Bad Guy" became the first song by an artist born in the 21st century to reach number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 and receive Diamond certification from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).

Eilish's second studio album, "Happier Than Ever" (2021), became her second album to debut at number one on the Billboard 200 and produced three US top-ten singles: "My Future", "Therefore I Am", and "Your Power". She won the Academy Award for Best Original Song for co-writing "No Time to Die" from the James Bond film "No Time to Die" (2021) and again for "What Was I Made For?" from the fantasy film "Barbie" (2023). Her third studio album, "Hit Me Hard and Soft" (2024), received critical acclaim and included the Billboard Global 200 number-one single "Birds of a Feather", which became the most-streamed solo song by a female artist on Spotify.

Eilish's accolades include two Academy Awards, ten Grammy Awards, nine American Music Awards, 20 Guinness World Records, eight MTV Video Music Awards, four Brit Awards and two Golden Globes. She became the second artist and the only woman in Grammy history to win all four general field categories, Record of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year and Best New Artist, at a single ceremony. She also became the youngest winner of Album of the Year and Record of the Year. Eilish was the first person born in the 21st century to win both a Grammy Award and an Academy Award and is the youngest person to win two Academy Awards. Her public activism has included campaigns and statements concerning climate change awareness, women's reproductive rights and gender equality.

Billie Eilish Pirate Baird O'Connell was born in Los Angeles, California, on December 18, 2001. She is the daughter of actress and teacher Maggie Baird and actor Patrick O'Connell, both of whom are also musicians and have worked on Eilish's tours. She is of Irish and Scottish descent. Her middle name, Eilish, was chosen by her parents after they watched a documentary about Irish conjoined twins Katie and Eilish Holton. It was originally intended to be her first name, while Pirate was intended to be her middle name. Her grandfather, William Baird, died while her mother was pregnant, and her parents subsequently named her after him. Eilish has said that she disliked her first name while growing up and would have preferred a name such as Violet, although she later came to identify strongly with the name Billie. She grew up in Los Angeles's Highland Park neighbourhood. Naturally blonde, she began dyeing her hair at the age of nine, initially using a blue Manic Panic shade, and has generally preferred black hair.

Eilish and her older brother, Finneas, were homeschooled by their mother. Their parents chose homeschooling in part to spend more time with their children and allow them greater freedom to pursue their interests. Baird taught both siblings the fundamentals of songwriting. Eilish has cited her brother and mother as influences on her interest in music. Their parents encouraged them to explore a range of interests, including art, dancing and acting.

Eilish began playing the ukulele at the age of six. She performed at talent shows and joined the Los Angeles Children's Chorus at the age of eight. At 11, she wrote her first song for her mother's songwriting class. The song concerned a zombie apocalypse and was inspired by the television series "The Walking Dead", from which Eilish used lines from scripts and episode titles. She participated in some acting auditions but disliked the process. She did, however, record background dialogue for crowd scenes and worked on the films "Diary of a Wimpy Kid", "Ramona and Beezus" and the "X-Men" series. She also took dance classes until 2016, when a growth plate injury ended her participation in dance and led her to focus on recording music.

In 2015, at the age of 13, Eilish began working on songs with her brother Finneas, who had already been writing and producing music for several years and had his own band. Among the first songs they recorded together were "She's Broken", written by Finneas, and "Fingers Crossed", written by Eilish. The siblings uploaded the recordings to SoundCloud.

On November 18, 2015, Eilish released "Ocean Eyes". The song was written, mixed and produced by Finneas, who had originally written it for his band the Slightlys before deciding that it suited Eilish's vocals. He gave the song to Eilish after her dance teacher, Fred Diaz, asked the siblings to write a song for choreography. They uploaded it to SoundCloud so that Diaz could access it. The recording attracted several hundred thousand plays within two weeks, leading Finneas's manager, Danny Rukasin, to discuss Eilish's potential as an artist.

In January 2016, Finneas and Rukasin arranged a deal through which Apple Music signed Eilish to A&R company Platoon, which specialised in developing emerging artists before major-label contracts. Eilish subsequently hired a publicist who connected her with the fashion brand Chanel and a stylist, contributing to the development of her public image. On March 24, 2016, a music video for "Ocean Eyes", directed by Megan Thompson, premiered on Eilish's official YouTube channel. The song and Eilish received promotion from various media outlets, radio stations and music industry figures. On June 23, 2016, Eilish and Finneas released "Six Feet Under" on SoundCloud as her second single. A homemade music video, directed by Eilish and edited by Maggie Baird, was released on June 30.

In August 2016, Justin Lubliner signed Eilish to Darkroom and Interscope Records. He developed her initial release strategy with an emphasis on establishing a distinct persona and aesthetic rather than relying on a single major hit. Darkroom and Interscope Records re-released "Six Feet Under" and "Ocean Eyes" as digital and streaming singles in November 2016. A dance performance video for "Ocean Eyes" was released on November 22.

In January 2017, Eilish released an EP containing four remixes of "Ocean Eyes" by Astronomyy, Blackbear, Goldhouse and Cautious Clay, followed by an EP of remixes of "Six Feet Under" by Blu J, Gazzo, Jerry Folk and Aire Atlantica. She subsequently released "Bellyache", followed by a music video directed by Miles and AJ. "Bored" was released as part of the soundtrack to the Netflix series "13 Reasons Why". Eilish also performed at the South by Southwest music festival in March 2017. She released "Watch" in June, followed by "Copycat" in July, and announced her debut EP, "Don't Smile at Me". She subsequently released "Idontwannabeyouanymore" and "My Boy". "Don't Smile at Me" was released on August 11, 2017, and reached number 14 on the US Billboard 200. Eilish supported the EP with the "Don't Smile at Me Tour" in October 2017. She released "Bitches Broken Hearts" through SoundCloud in November.

Eilish's music was promoted by Spotify, including through its "Today's Top Hits" playlist. Critics described her early sound as melancholic pop influenced by artists including Lana Del Rey and incorporating elements of hip-hop production. In September 2017, Apple Music named Eilish its Up Next artist. The promotion included a short documentary, a live session EP and an interview with Zane Lowe on Beats 1. The live EP, "Up Next Session: Billie Eilish", was released that month. In December, Eilish released "&Burn", a collaboration with American rapper Vince Staples and a remix of "Watch", which appeared on the expanded edition of "Don't Smile at Me".

In February 2018, Eilish embarked on the "Where's My Mind Tour", which concluded in April. "Bitches Broken Hearts" was re-released worldwide in March. For Record Store Day 2018, Eilish released "Party Favor" on pink 7-inch vinyl, accompanied by a cover of Drake's "Hotline Bling" as the B-side. She collaborated with American singer Khalid on "Lovely", released in April and included on the soundtrack of the second season of "13 Reasons Why". She released "You Should See Me in a Crown" in July and performed at the Mo Pop Festival that month.

Eilish released "When the Party's Over" in October 2018 and subsequently embarked on the "1 by 1 Tour", which concluded in March 2019. In October 2018, she signed a talent contract with Next Management for fashion and beauty endorsements. She was included on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in November and released "Come Out and Play", which had been written for a holiday-themed Apple advertisement.

In January 2019, "Don't Smile at Me" surpassed one billion streams on Spotify. That month, Eilish released "Bury a Friend", the third single from her debut studio album, "When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?", as well as "When I Was Older", a song inspired by the 2018 film "Roma" that appeared on the compilation album "Music Inspired by the Film Roma". In February, she participated in the YouTube documentary miniseries "A Snippet Into Billie's Mind". "Wish You Were Gay", the fourth single from the album, was released in March.

"When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?" was released on March 29, 2019. The album debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and UK Albums Chart, making Eilish the first artist born in the 2000s to have a number-one album in the United States and the youngest female artist to have a number-one album in the United Kingdom. Following its release, Eilish set a record for the most simultaneously charting songs on the US Billboard Hot 100 by a female artist, with 14. "Bad Guy" was released as the album's fifth single and subsequently became her first US number-one single. A remix featuring Justin Bieber was released in July 2019. In August, "Bad Guy" reached number one in the United States, ending Lil Nas X's 19-week run at the top of the chart with "Old Town Road". Eilish became the first artist born in the 2000s and the youngest artist since Lorde to have a US number-one single.

Eilish began the "When We All Fall Asleep Tour" at the Coachella Festival in April 2019, concluding the tour in Mexico City in November. In August, she participated in Apple's "Music Lab: Remix Billie Eilish", in which fans could deconstruct "You Should See Me in a Crown" and create remixes using Apple devices and GarageBand. In September, she announced the "Where Do We Go? World Tour". The tour began in Miami in March 2020 but was cancelled after three shows because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

In November 2019, Third Man Records announced plans to release an acoustic live album documenting Eilish's performance at the label's Blue Room. That month, she released "Everything I Wanted". She received six Grammy Award nominations for the 2020 ceremony, including Record of the Year and Song of the Year for "Bad Guy", Album of the Year and Best New Artist. At 17, she became the youngest artist to receive nominations in all four general field categories. Billboard named her its Woman of the Year for 2019.

In January 2020, Eilish was announced as the performer of the title song for the James Bond film "No Time to Die", which she wrote and produced with Finneas. She became the youngest artist to write and perform a James Bond theme. The song became the second Bond theme to top the UK singles chart and the first performed by a female artist to do so. At the 62nd Annual Grammy Awards, Eilish won the four main Grammy categories: Best New Artist, Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Album of the Year, becoming the youngest person to achieve the feat at a single ceremony.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Eilish and Finneas performed for the "Living Room Concert for America" and "Together at Home" concert series, with proceeds and publicity supporting efforts related to the pandemic. "Ilomilo" was released to Italian contemporary hit radio in April 2020 as the final single from "When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?". In July, Eilish released "My Future", accompanied by an animated video. She became the youngest person to appear on the Forbes Celebrity 100 list, with reported earnings of $53 million. In September, she released a collection of branded ukuleles in collaboration with Fender.

In October 2020, Eilish staged the virtual concert "Where Do We Go? The Livestream" in Los Angeles. The performance used extended reality technology and featured Finneas and drummer Andrew Marshall. Ticket proceeds supported touring crew members affected by cancellations during the COVID-19 pandemic. That month, Eilish said she was working on new material. She won three Billboard Music Awards in October, including Top Female Artist and Top Billboard 200 Album for "When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?". She released "Therefore I Am" in November and performed "Therefore I Am" and "My Future" at the Jingle Ball in December.

In January 2021, Eilish released "Lo Vas a Olvidar", a collaboration with Rosalía for the HBO series "Euphoria". On February 26, the documentary film "Billie Eilish: The World's a Little Blurry", directed by R. J. Cutler, was released on Apple TV+ and in selected cinemas. The film documents Eilish's personal life and career during her rise to prominence. At the 63rd Annual Grammy Awards, she won Best Song Written for Visual Media for "No Time to Die" and Record of the Year for "Everything I Wanted". In 2021, she also published "By Billie Eilish", a book of photographs selected by her.

In April 2021, Eilish announced her second studio album, "Happier Than Ever", which was released on July 30. It was preceded by the singles "My Future", "Therefore I Am", "Your Power", "Lost Cause" and "NDA" and was accompanied by the title track. The album was issued in multiple formats, including collectible vinyl and cassette editions. In December, Eilish announced a limited-edition vinyl edition made from recycled vinyl scraps, available through selected Gucci stores and accompanied by Gucci-branded nail stickers designed by Alessandro Michele.

To promote "Happier Than Ever", Eilish worked with Disney+ on the concert film "Happier Than Ever: A Love Letter to Los Angeles", released in September 2021. She began the "Happier Than Ever, The World Tour" in February 2022, concluding it in April 2023. In December 2022, she performed three concerts titled "Happier Than Ever, The Hometown Encore" at the Kia Forum in Inglewood, California.

In June 2021, Eilish faced criticism after videos circulated in which she appeared to mouth an anti-Asian slur while lip-syncing to Tyler, the Creator's song "Fish". Matthew Tyler Vorce, who was reported to be her boyfriend at the time, also received criticism over alleged social media posts containing offensive language and slurs. Eilish faced further criticism over accusations of queerbaiting following the use of the caption "I love girls" in promotion for the music video for "Lost Cause". Eilish apologised for her use of the slur, stating that she had been 13 or 14 at the time and had not understood its derogatory meaning. She also addressed a separate video that had been interpreted as mocking an Asian accent, explaining that she had been using an invented voice. In a later interview, she discussed changes in her views since adolescence and the permanence of material posted online.

Eilish began developing material for her third studio album with Finneas in December 2021. In 2022, she won the Academy Award for Best Original Song for "No Time to Die", becoming the first person born in the 21st century to win an Academy Award. She also became the youngest headliner of the Glastonbury and Coachella festivals. For the Pixar film "Turning Red", she and Finneas wrote three songs, "Nobody Like U", "U Know What's Up" and "1 True Love", performed by the fictional boy band 4*Town.

In June 2022, Eilish performed the then-unreleased song "TV" during a concert in Manchester. The song references the overturning of Roe v. Wade, the US Supreme Court decision that had established a constitutional right to abortion in the United States. In July, she released the two-track EP "Guitar Songs", consisting of "TV" and "The 30th". Eilish said she wanted to release the songs without waiting for her third studio album because she considered their subject matter particularly current. She also expressed a preference for releasing music with less traditional promotion, similar to the approach she had taken earlier in her career.

Eilish worked with Apple Music to release a film documenting one of her "Happier Than Ever" concerts at the O2 Arena in London. She described the film as an opportunity for people who had been unable to obtain tickets to experience the tour. The "Happier Than Ever, The Hometown Encore" concerts were held at the Kia Forum in December 2022.

In 2023, Eilish made her acting debut in the Amazon Prime Video satirical thriller series "Swarm". She played Eva, the leader of a cult inspired by NXIVM. Her performance received positive reviews. Eilish and Finneas wrote "What Was I Made For?" for the soundtrack of the 2023 film "Barbie". Eilish said that unfinished scenes from the film inspired the song. In 2024, the song won the Academy Award for Best Original Song and two Grammy Awards, for Song of the Year and Best Song Written for Visual Media. It became the tenth song to win both the Academy Award for Best Original Song and the Grammy Award for Song of the Year. Eilish became the youngest person to win two Academy Awards.

On April 8, 2024, Eilish announced her third studio album, "Hit Me Hard and Soft", which was released on May 17. In April, she was announced as the featured artist for the video game "Fortnite Festival", with an unlockable outfit based on her appearance. While in London to promote the album, she appeared on the web series "Chicken Shop Date" with Amelia Dimoldenberg and as a guest host for the children's television channel CBeebies' bedtime story programme. In August, Eilish appeared on a remix of Charli XCX's "Guess", from the deluxe edition of the album "Brat". The accompanying video included scenes of Eilish and Charli XCX surrounded by piles of women's underwear, which was subsequently donated to the charity I Support the Girls. On August 11, Eilish performed "Birds of a Feather" during the closing ceremony of the 2024 Summer Olympics in Long Beach, California, as part of the handover to Los Angeles, the host city of the 2028 Summer Olympics. She subsequently embarked on the "Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour", which comprised 106 concerts across North America, Oceania, Europe and Asia between September 2024 and November 2025.

In March 2026, it was reported that Eilish was in advanced negotiations to make her feature film acting debut as Esther Greenwood in a Sarah Polley-directed adaptation of Sylvia Plath's novel "The Bell Jar". Eilish's concert film "Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour (Live in 3D)", which she co-directed and produced with James Cameron, was theatrically released on May 8, 2026.

The lead single “Paint the Town Red” topped the Billboard Hot 100 and the Billboard Global 200. Her fifth studio album, “Vie” (2025), included a return to pop influences and also reached the top five. Doja Cat has sold millions of records worldwide and has received numerous awards and nominations, including a Grammy Award. He was named one of the 100 most influential people in the world by Time magazine in 2023. On July 17, 2026, he released his third studio album, Oh Yeah?. 2. Steven Norman Lackritz (born July 23, 1934 – died June 4, 2004), better known as Steve Lacy, was an American jazz saxophonist and composer recognized as one of the important players of soprano saxophone. Coming to prominence in the 1950s as a progressive dixieland musician, Lacy went on to a long and prolific career. He worked extensively in experimental jazz and to a lesser extent in free improvisation, but Lacy's music was typically melodic and tightly-structured. Lacy also became a highly distinctive composer, with compositions often built out of little more than a single questioning phrase, repeated several times. After Lacy was diagnosed with cancer in August 2003, he continued playing and teaching until his death on June 4, 2004 at the age of 69. Read more on Last.fm.
